title: OPERATION PATIENT YOKE
skeleton: occupier must restart quota production stopped by disciplined passive resistance before an industrial heat clock makes the loss irreversible, while every coercion deepens the stoppage and the only working lever is a labor hierarchy the occupier is forbidden to recognize
inspiration: Franco-Belgian occupation of the Ruhr and the German passive resistance, 1923
situation: {WORLD} fell to {EMPLOYER} in {YEAR} with its factories undamaged. That was the point of taking it. The Vossberg Castings Combine in {DISTRICT} makes {castingQuota} tons of endo-steel structural parts every 30 days, and your Clan's whole rebuild plan for the next campaign depends on that number. Taking the world cost 4 warriors. Holding it is now costing the quota. Eleven days ago a merchant-caste administrator cut the workers' food ration by one-fifth to save money. The workers did not riot. They did something the warrior caste has no answer for: 41,000 of them show up on time, run every machine strictly by the written rules, file every safety complaint the manuals allow, and produce only {productionPct} percent of quota. No law is broken. There is nothing to shoot. A hidden committee runs the slowdown. {NPC:intel-source}, your Watch liaison, estimates 9 secret groups of 3 to 5 organizers each, but their names are unconfirmed and the report is 6 days old, so treat it as a rough guess. The committee even prints the shortfall numbers on leaflets before the administration can publish them. The real danger is heat. The No. 2 casting furnace runs nonstop and was never built to sit idle. The slowdown has already cut its metal feed to the bare minimum. If the furnace goes cold, restarting it takes 70 days and a specialist repair crew shipped in from off-world — and the cycle quota fails for good. The terrain problem is the Vossberg funicular: a single steep ore railway, 7.2 kilometers long on a 28-degree slope, and the only way to haul bulk ore from the Kettling mines to the foundry. On day 9 a work shift peacefully occupied the upper funicular station and laid their tools out for inspection. Clearing them by force would take Elementals 20 minutes and stop all ore movement for the season, because the winch house cannot survive a fight and all 3 of the planet's trained winch crews are sitting inside it. Your {FORCE_SIZE} governs {DISTRICT}. The Galaxy commander's order is one sentence: meet the cycle quota. The administrator who cut the ration outranks you in caste and has filed a formal protest against undoing it. Through {NPC:intel-source}, the committee has offered a deal: full work resumes if you restore the old ration and recognize an elected workers' council. The Clan caste system has no place for such a council.

objectives.primary: Get Vossberg Castings back to full output — 100 percent of the {castingQuota}-ton cycle quota — before the cycle ends at T+480:00.
objectives.secondary: Keep the No. 2 casting furnace hot enough to run the whole time. It must never go cold.
objectives.bonus: Identify all 9 committee groups — names and structure — without mass arrests, and hand the Watch a verified list.

complications.name: The Heat Clock
complications.text: The No. 2 casting furnace cools toward the point of no return whenever staffing drops below 60 percent of a full shift. At the current slowdown, it hits that point in {furnaceMargin} hours. Restarting a cold furnace takes 70 days and a repair crew from off-world.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A countdown timer is visible from the start. Any garrison action that pulls workers off the foundry floor — arrests, lockouts, cordons — speeds the countdown up by 6 hours for every 1,000 workers affected. If it hits zero, the furnace is dead: the primary objective can no longer be met and the mission locks into the FAILURE outcome.

complications.name: The Funicular Station
complications.text: The occupied winch house is the only path for ore, and it holds the only 3 trained winch crews on the planet. Engineers say the building cannot survive weapons fire of any kind.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any combat inside the station's map hex wrecks the winch house, stopping ore flow for the rest of the mission and turning 1,400 peaceful occupiers into active fighters. Entering by agreement or without a fight keeps both the ore flow and the crews.

complications.name: The Administrator's Standing
complications.text: The ration cut is a lawful merchant-caste decision. You can overrule it by warrior command, but doing so breaks the balance of caste power across the whole occupation zone. Four other world administrators have said they will file a joint protest to the Galaxy's chief merchant.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If you restore the ration by command, the merchant caste turns cold: every merchant-cooperation check in this mission and later missions in the zone takes one penalty step for 90 days.

complications.name: Stay-Behind Opportunists
complications.text: A leftover Inner Sphere militia cell is trying to turn the peaceful slowdown into sabotage. Its strength is unconfirmed — we only know it exists because 2 weapons caches turned up when we took the world. The committee has refused to work with it so far, but one garrison atrocity would change that overnight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every time the garrison escalates (see The Heat Clock), the saboteur cell gets one free hidden strike against foundry equipment during the mission.

decisionPoints.name: The Lever
decisionPoints.context: The committee's offer runs out when the heat clock does. The Galaxy commander will give no guidance; the record will show only what you chose. You have three tools, and each one sends a lasting message to the whole occupation zone about how the Clan handles defiance.

options.title: Treat Through the Liaison
advantages: Work restarts within 24 to 36 hours — inside the heat-clock deadline
The winch house reopens without a fight, saving the funicular and its 3 crews
{NPC:intel-source} gains standing access to the committee, opening a permanent intelligence source
disadvantages: The record now shows the Clan bargaining with an elected workers' council
The administrator files a formal grievance, and the chief merchant sides with them
Every district in the zone learns that a disciplined slowdown can move a Galaxy commander's quota
options.consequence: Output recovers to 96 percent by the cycle's end. Within 60 days, 3 more worlds in the zone form councils and make the same demands, and the Khan's anger arrives addressed to your unit by name.

costs.resource: HONOR — your codex records that you bargained with defiant workers instead of mastering them
costs.risk: Other worlds copy this: zone-wide council demands within 60 days, which raise the difficulty of later missions

options.title: Import Replacement Crews
advantages: No bargaining, no council, no example set — Clan doctrine holds firm
Technician-caste crews from the navy's storage yards can keep the furnace hot
The committee loses its power once the foundry runs without its own workers
disadvantages: The 21-day trip strips the sister garrison on Hyner of its repair unit
The furnace goes cold before the crews arrive, unless you break part of the slowdown anyway
The imported crews can only run the furnace at 40 percent, not 100 — so the quota still fails this cycle
options.consequence: The furnace survives but the quota falls short by about half. The slowdown hardens into a year-long standoff the whole zone watches. The committee is never broken and becomes a permanent hidden power.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — you give up the sister garrison's repair unit for 90 days, dropping their readiness one level
costs.risk: A 50-percent quota shortfall is logged against your unit in the Galaxy record

options.title: Arrest the Committee
advantages: Arresting all 9 groups in one night removes the brain that coordinates the slowdown
It proves that following the rules is no shield for organized defiance
The administrator keeps their authority, and the balance of caste power stays intact
disadvantages: The list of who is in each group is 6 days old and only a rough guess — raid the wrong homes and you create martyrs
Arrests pull workers and witnesses off the floor, so the heat clock speeds up by 18 hours
The stay-behind saboteur cell gets its recruiting argument and its free strikes
options.consequence: You take 4 to 7 of the 9 groups. The slowdown loses its coordination but gains rage: output rises to 61 percent under guard, sabotage starts within a month, and the bonus objective is lost for good.

costs.resource: ISORLA — the bonus list is lost, and the Watch marks your intelligence network as burned
costs.risk: Heat clock drops 18 hours at once; a sabotage campaign is seeded into later missions

entries.event: ALARM — the upper funicular station is occupied; ore stops flowing to the foundry.
The No. 2 furnace starts eating its stored ore reserve; its metal feed drops to 55 percent.
The ore reserve runs out. The heat-clock countdown to a cold furnace begins ({furnaceMargin} hours left).
The committee's leaflets report your response across all 6 worker districts, whatever you chose.
The Galaxy commander's aide arrives to review the quota and examine what you have done so far.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The furnace goes cold at T+36:00 plus {furnaceMargin} hours. After that, no decision can save the cycle quota, and the mission is graded on whatever output remains.

opforSketch.composition: No normal enemy force at the start. The opposition is 41,000 unarmed, disciplined workers on a peaceful slowdown. There is also one stay-behind militia cell: plan against 20 to 40 fighters with small arms, mining charges, and 2 to 3 light utility vehicles rigged for sabotage. Combat only happens if the garrison escalates.
opforSketch.behavior: The committee avoids all provocation and records every garrison act. The saboteur cell attacks only equipment, only after the garrison escalates, and never holds ground. There is no army to beat here — only a choice of how hard to push.

forks.name: OPERATION KEPT FLAME
forks.trigger: Quota met and the furnace never went cold.
forks.consequence: The district becomes the zone's showcase, which makes it a target. Real saboteurs — not the committee — begin a precise campaign against the foundry, and the garrison must now defend it while keeping output at full.

forks.name: OPERATION LEAN SEASON
forks.trigger: The furnace went cold, or the quota failed by more than a third.
forks.consequence: With production gone, the food ration collapses too. Hunger does what the peaceful committee would not: the garrison now faces riots across 6 worker districts during the 70-day furnace repair.

forks.name: OPERATION ROOT AND BRANCH
forks.trigger: Mass arrests or weapons fire inside the foundry during the slowdown.
forks.consequence: The committee's survivors accept the stay-behind cell's offer. Within 90 days an armed underground with 41,000 supporters operates from the mine tunnels, and the garrison's real war begins.

storyElementSeed: In the foundry canteen, a warrior watches a worker fill out a machine-fault form in perfect, careful handwriting. The worker presses hard so the third copy stays legible. The warrior realizes the form is the weapon.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Restore Vossberg Castings to full quota before the cycle ends. The Commonwealth judges this garrison two ways: by tons delivered and by bad headlines avoided. Deliver on both.

merc.decisionPoints[0].context: The employer wants the quota met and wants clean hands, in that order — but the contract's labor-dispute clause pays extra for neither. Whatever you choose, get the price agreed in writing before you act.

castingQuota.unit: tons of endo-steel members per 30-day cycle

furnaceMargin.unit: hours from reserve exhaustion to relining threshold

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no dropships in the system, so the replacement crews must travel on a hired merchant ship — 34 days instead of 21. The furnace goes cold long before they arrive, so this option cannot save the quota by itself.

title: OPERATION LIVE CIRCLE
skeleton: a graded rehearsal must finish by its fixed date while a real enemy hunts inside the exercise box, and every safety constraint that makes it training marks the trainees as prey
situation: The Varga Sound mudflats on {WORLD} were chosen as the final exercise ground for a sibko — a group of warrior cadets raised and trained together — because the ground punishes any mistake. It is 30 kilometers of flooded river delta where the tide reshapes the channels twice a day. Only 2 paved exit lanes carry a 'Mech's weight at every tide: the Stone Road on the north shore and the Causey Hards to the southeast. Everything between them is graded, dangerous ground. {EMPLOYER} needs the final exercise finished by T+54:00, because that is when the convoy leaves for the cadets' Trial of Position — the combat test that decides which warriors earn front-line 'Mechs. This cycle's new OmniMechs are promised to the Galaxy whose cadets score best, so results matter. Cadets who miss the convoy are not rescheduled; they are simply reassigned to lesser duty. You command the instructors: a Star of older second-line 'Mechs and 3 Elemental Points (Clan battle-armor infantry), average warrior age 51, running graded lanes for {cadetMechs} cadet 'Mechs set up for training. On each cadet 'Mech, 2 of its 4 weapon groups are loaded with dummy rounds, its transponder broadcasts an exercise ID, and its radio is locked to training channels. At T+0 an instructor's Wasp was destroyed on Lane 2. The grading computer logged it as a scripted umpire kill. It was not. Wreck analysis confirms real autocannon fire — Inner Sphere 80mm rounds. A raiding force is inside the exercise area. {NPC:intel-source} believes it is what remains of a House deep-raid company that hid after the invasion passed: {raiderMechs} fast light and medium 'Mechs, plus 2 infantry platoons carrying inferno launchers and mines. These are veterans who have studied the exercise schedule for weeks. That report is only 2 hours old — treat their exact strength as an estimate, but their presence is confirmed. They also hold 3 stolen umpire transponders (a rough count, based on missing beacon serial numbers), so on cadet screens their 'Mechs show up as harmless umpires. Their goal was clear within the first hour: they are not here to raid the depot. They are hunting the cadets — the future warriors of a Clan — scattered across 3 lanes in 'Mechs that can only fire half their weapons, crewed by warriors who have never been shot at for real. The enemy DropShip waiting beyond the sound is estimated to lift in about {liftWindow} hours. The Trial convoy will not wait. The mudflats do not care either way.

objectives.primary: Keep the cadets alive — zero cadet deaths — while destroying or driving off the raiding force inside the exercise area.
objectives.secondary: Finish the graded exercise in a form the Trial judges will certify by T+54:00.
objectives.bonus: Capture the raid commander, or take one raider 'Mech intact as war-spoils, and recover the stolen umpire transponders.

complications.name: Exercise Loadouts
complications.text: Cadet 'Mechs carry dummy rounds in 2 of their 4 weapon groups, and their energy weapons are set to low training power. They can only get real ammunition at the range depot on the Stone Road, which takes 40 minutes to rearm one Star even under an emergency drill.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Cadet units fight at half weapon strength until they pass through the depot. The depot rearms only one Star at a time, so deciding the order of the queue matters.

complications.name: Stolen Umpire Beacons
complications.text: The 3 raider 'Mechs carrying stolen transponders show up as harmless umpires on every cadet's screen. Instructor 'Mechs hold the code that reveals the truth, but they can only pass it one cadet at a time, by line-of-sight laser link, lane by lane.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until an instructor has linked with a cadet this mission, that cadet cannot target-lock the beacon-carrying raiders, and those raiders can close in without the cadet being cleared to fire.

complications.name: The Tide
complications.text: Twice a day, the rising tide floods the channels between lanes for 4 hours. A 'Mech caught between the paved lanes when the water rises must stand still, exposed, and wait — or risk sinking into the mud and needing a winch to get out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Show the tide schedule at the start. During each flood, 'Mechs over 40 tons cannot move between lanes. The raiders' infantry crosses anyway, using skimmers.

complications.name: Cadet Eagerness
complications.text: These cadets are 6 weeks from their Trial and have been graded on aggression their whole lives. Once one of them scores a real kill, every cadet on the radio net will want the next one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any cadet Star that spots a raider must pass a discipline check or leave its assigned lane to chase — walking straight into the ambush the raiders set behind the bait.

decisionPoints.name: The Instructor's Choice
decisionPoints.context: At T+1:10 you hold the radio net. The cadets are spread across 3 lanes, half-armed, and their screens show the enemy as umpires. The Trial convoy lifts at T+54:00 whether or not results are certified. Clan doctrine has no rule for this, and your codex will record whatever you order next.

options.title: Abort and Shield the Cadets
advantages: The cadets pull back to the Stone Road depot behind the instructor Star — the Clan's future warriors are safe within 3 hours
Your instructors fight the raiders with veteran skill and full weapons, on ground you chose
No half-armed cadet is ever in a raider's sights again
disadvantages: The exercise is canceled — no certified results reach the Trial convoy
The whole sibko misses its Trial cycle, and their promised new 'Mechs go to a rival Galaxy instead
One aging Star and 3 Points against a veteran company is a fair fight, not a safe one
options.consequence: The cadets live but go ungraded. Their Trial slips a full cycle, and about a third of them will age out into infantry duty. Your codex records the choice: the instructors who put the children ahead of the Clan's schedule.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — this cycle's new OmniMechs are lost to a rival Galaxy
costs.risk: HONOR — codex entry: canceled a Trial cycle; the sibko's failure rate becomes your unit's legacy

options.title: Convert the Exercise
advantages: The exercise becomes real: cadets hunt the raiders while instructors grade them — the truest test any judge could ask for
Once the cadets rearm at the depot, numbers favor the Clan
Cadets who survive real combat against veterans enter their Trial with experience no drill can teach
disadvantages: Cadets will die. Veterans with infernos and mines do not go easy
Because of the rearm queue, the first fights are still fought at half weapon strength
This is exactly what the raiders want: scattered cadets chasing bait into prepared kill zones
options.consequence: You lose 2 to 5 cadets before the area is cleared. The survivors score a full grade above the usual sibko results, and the Galaxy argues for years over whether the trade was mastery or waste.

costs.resource: LIVES STAKED — expect to lose 2 to 5 cadets and their 'Mechs, weighed against Trial results one grade above normal
costs.risk: If the raiders' ambush holds, losses double and the FAILURE outcome arms

options.title: Screen the Cadets and Finish the Course
advantages: Instructors form a fighting screen along the lane edges while cadets complete shortened graded lanes inside it
Certified results reach the convoy at T+54:00 — the Trial deadline holds
The cadets never fight the raiders at all
disadvantages: One Star and 3 Points cannot seal 30 kilometers of tidal flat, so the screen has gaps — and the raiders read the tides better than the training plan does
Your instructors take every fight alone, badly outnumbered, for 2 days
If the screen breaks even once, half-armed cadets meet veterans mid-lane with no instructor near enough to help
options.consequence: The course finishes. Your instructors spend themselves holding the line — 40 to 60 percent instructor casualties — and the cadets certify on schedule, graded by warriors who were dying one lane over.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — the instructor Star fights with no relief; plan for 40 to 60 percent instructor casualties
costs.risk: One gap in the screen puts raiders among half-armed cadets, and the primary objective fails within minutes

entries.event: ALARM — an instructor Wasp is destroyed on Lane 2 by real fire logged as an umpire kill.
Wreck analysis confirms real Inner Sphere autocannon fire. The exercise net is still running; the cadets do not know.
A serial-number check shows 3 umpire transponders missing. You must decide what to order.
The next flood tide covers the channels between lanes for 4 hours. Movement between lanes stops.
Best estimate of when the raiders' DropShip lifts ({liftWindow} hours from T+0).
The Trial convoy lifts. Certified results are aboard, or the cycle is lost.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hard deadline T+54:00. The Trial convoy lifts at that exact hour and will not wait for weather, casualties, or any other reason. If the cadets' graded results are not certified and physically aboard by then, the whole sibko misses its Trial cycle. There is no rescheduling and no late submission.

opforSketch.composition: Veteran Inner Sphere deep-raid survivors: {raiderMechs} fast light/medium 'Mechs (around 35 tons on average), 2 infantry platoons with inferno SRMs, command-detonated mines, and 3 stolen umpire transponders. No supply line; one hidden DropShip somewhere beyond the sound.
opforSketch.behavior: They ambush constantly: bait with a beacon-carrying 'Mech, kill the pursuer in a prepared zone, then move before the tide turns. They refuse all stand-up fights, target instructors first when they can, and fight only to make their DropShip lift — not to the death.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY BERTH
forks.trigger: The area is cleared with the cadets intact and results certified.
forks.consequence: Questioning prisoners locates the raiders' DropShip at a tidal anchorage 60 kilometers north, waiting for a second raider team still at large. Your unit is closest. Take the ship before it lifts.

forks.name: OPERATION RECLAIMED SEED
forks.trigger: Cadets killed or captured, or the raiders escape with prisoners.
forks.consequence: The raiders lift off with 2 captured cadets and stolen cases of Clan genetic samples from the exercise infirmary. Your Clan must reach them before their JumpShip leaves the system — or before an Inner Sphere spy agency takes delivery.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG SHADOW
forks.trigger: The exercise was canceled, or the Trial judges rejected the results.
forks.consequence: The ungraded cadets are held on garrison duty while their case is reviewed, and your unit serves beside them under a Watch observer who reports every day. Every patrol is a test your unit is quietly failing.

storyElementSeed: On the depot apron, a cadet stands by the rearm gantry and holds out a dummy autocannon round to an instructor twice her age. Her eyes ask whether the next round will be real.

is-davion.decisionPoints[0].context: Training command will back whatever the senior instructor calls, and write it up either way. The cadets are half-armed, the hostiles are veterans, and the graduation board convenes in 54 hours. Nobody is coming to make this call for you.

liftWindow.unit: hours to estimated raider DropShip lift

resourceGates.lackingText: The range depot does not have enough live ammunition for a full rearm, so the cadets fight the whole mission at half weapon strength. Expected cadet losses rise from 2-5 to 4-8.

title: OPERATION DARK LATTICE
skeleton: security force must climb a compartmented cell pyramid before a fixed ceremonial date while every effective policing instrument alienates the population that is the campaign's true prize, and the force's own doctrine names the work beneath it
inspiration: Battle of Algiers and the quadrillage system, 1957
situation: Six bombs in 40 days. The seventh went off this morning at the {DISTRICT} caste registry hall on {WORLD}: 2 warriors dead, 31 civilians dead, the records archive burned. {EMPLOYER} took this world in {YEAR} and has ruled it fairly — fair quotas, no reprisals — and the bombs keep coming anyway. The bombers understand what the garrison will not admit: this is a war for the people watching, and every blast says the Clan cannot protect what it rules. The bombing network is built as a secret pyramid, with each level cut off from the others. {NPC:intel-source} of the Watch (your Clan's intelligence service) estimates {networkCells} cells of 3 people each. Each cell knows only one courier above it and nothing about the others. Couriers change on a 72-hour rhythm. The bombs are military shaped charges from a pre-conquest militia depot; the recovered stock list shows {chargesOutstanding} charges still missing, though that count is unconfirmed. The whole network assessment is 8 days old, so treat it as a rough guess. The terrain problem is the Old Lattice: 14 square kilometers of pre-war arcade city — stacked shopping galleries, raised walkways, and cellars — where most of the capital lives and works. Elementals (Clan battle-armor infantry) can enter the Lattice, but they cannot chase anyone through it without collapsing a century of jury-rigged construction onto 9,000 shopkeepers. That collapse is exactly the picture the network wants the world to see. The deadline is fixed and cannot move. In 19 days the conquest-day ceremony is held in Unity Plaza at the Lattice's edge, attended by the Khan's representative and 40,000 civilians ordered to be there. Canceling it would be the Clan publicly admitting defeat. The network's leaflets have promised an attack worthy of the day. The garrison's tools are all wrong for this job. Warriors do not do police work; the local police force inherited from the old government leaks (2 confirmed leaks in 60 days); and the methods that would crack the pyramid fastest are the ones a Crusader rival on the Galaxy staff is waiting to condemn as dezgra — dishonorable — in open council. Your {FORCE_SIZE} holds the capital. Whoever sits at the top of the pyramid ({NPC:opfor-commander}) holds the initiative, with 19 days of it left.

objectives.primary: Break the bombing network before the conquest-day ceremony at T+456:00: take down its leadership and account for the missing charges.
objectives.secondary: Hold the ceremony in Unity Plaza on schedule, with zero bombs going off inside the security zone.
objectives.bonus: Capture the network's leader alive and unharmed — fit to be assessed as a bondsman (a captive taken into Clan service) rather than executed.

complications.name: The Leaky Police Force
complications.text: The old civilian police are the only people who know the streets, and they leak. Two operations shared with police liaisons in the last 60 days were blown within a day.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any plan you share with the police reaches the network in 24 to 48 hours. Any plan you run without them takes one penalty step on all city-search tasks, because you lack local knowledge.

complications.name: The Old Lattice
complications.text: The Lattice is a multi-level arcade city — fragile, vital to the economy, and packed with civilians 18 hours a day. The network's couriers blend in as locals. The garrison stands out as a slow, watched intruder.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 'Mechs cannot enter the Lattice. If an Elemental chases someone inside and fails a movement check, part of the structure collapses. Each collapse adds one permanent penalty step to all population-cooperation rolls.

complications.name: The Immovable Date
complications.text: The ceremony happens on the conquest anniversary or it is a defeat. The Khan's representative has refused, in writing, to even consider delaying it. And 40,000 civilians packed into one plaza is a target the network can count just as easily as you can.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The mission ends at T+456:00 no matter what state the network is in. Every objective is graded against that hour, and there is no extension at any price.

complications.name: The Watching Rival
complications.text: A Crusader Star Colonel on the Galaxy staff is filing reports on your methods. Harsh interrogations, mass arrests, or civilian deaths all become evidence they can use against you in a formal hearing of your peers.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each method judged dezgra (dishonorable) gives the rival one point against you. At 3 points, the COMPROMISED outcome arms no matter how the operation itself goes.

decisionPoints.name: The Method
decisionPoints.context: Nineteen days. A pyramid of {networkCells} cells, one captured courier in your cells, and a city watching how the Clan hunts. In the time left, the Watch can fully support only one main method. The other two can only be run as small side efforts, if at all.

options.title: Build the Grid
advantages: Register every sector, issue movement passes, count people block by block: for the first time since the conquest, you can actually read the Lattice
Couriers on a 72-hour cycle cannot keep moving through a gridded city without eventually showing up in the numbers
The system outlasts the mission — every future security job inherits it
disadvantages: It takes 12 days to set up, and the network operates freely during all 12
Warriors checking work passes in stairwells is exactly the picture the rival's file wants
The grid touches every civilian every day, so anger builds in the very population you are fighting for
options.consequence: By day 14 the courier pattern shows up in the numbers and 2 cells fall. You can truly seal the plaza. But the city's resentment deepens by one permanent step, and the network's surviving levels go quiet — undefeated, now cataloged, and waiting.

costs.resource: TIME — 12 of your 19 days used up before any result; expect 2 bombings during setup
costs.risk: HONOR — the rival's file gets its first piece of evidence: warriors doing police work

options.title: Turn the Courier
advantages: The captured courier knows one contact above him. Offer him a place as a bondsman and you can climb the pyramid one link at a time
It is fast — each level falls in 3 to 5 days as long as the trail holds
No grid, no mass measures, and nothing for the rival's file
disadvantages: You are following a single trail. If the courier is a double agent, your hunt leads the network straight to you
Taking a bomber into Clan service as a bondsman is itself something the rival can attack you for in council
Every link you roll up warns the level above to speed up the ceremony attack
options.consequence: The trail climbs 2 levels in 9 days, then hits a cut-off point and goes dead. You are left with a half-broken network on a deadline, deciding whether to call off the ceremony attack or move it up to day 15.

costs.resource: HONOR — a confessed bomber joins the bondsman roll with your commander's name as his sponsor
costs.risk: If the courier is a double agent, the network learns your hunt pattern and moves the ceremony attack up 4 days

options.title: Raid the Suspected Sites
advantages: Hit the 3 best-known sites this week, all at once, with Elementals, using the intelligence you already have
Speed beats the courier cycle — anything you seize is seized before word can spread
Decisive if the intelligence is right: the network's leaders may be among the 3
disadvantages: The intelligence is 8 days old and only a rough guess, so wrong doors in the Lattice mean collapses and dead civilians
Three raids into the arcade city is the network's dream propaganda whether the raids succeed or fail
Anyone you miss scatters, and the pyramid rebuilds after the ceremony — hostile and now wiser
options.consequence: The raids take 1 site cleanly, find 1 empty, and collapse a gallery floor at the third — 9 civilians dead. The network loses a level but gains a recruiting story it will use for years.

costs.resource: ISORLA — the civilian deaths void the bonus objective and drop population cooperation one permanent step
costs.risk: Two of the three sites are likely wrong at current confidence — that risk is built into the gallery collapse

entries.event: ALARM — seventh bomb at the {DISTRICT} caste registry hall. 33 dead. Network leaflets promise an attack for conquest day.
The Watch predicts the network's next movement window, based on its 72-hour courier rhythm.
The rival Star Colonel's first report on your methods reaches the Galaxy staff.
The security zone around Unity Plaza must be declared and sealed for an advance sweep.
The Khan's representative lands. All security postures lock in place.
The conquest-day ceremony begins, with 40,000 civilians present.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+456:00. The ceremony is held on the anniversary or the Clan publicly admits defeat. Every plan is graded against that hour, and there is no later chance.

opforSketch.composition: A hidden urban network: {networkCells} cells of 3 (27 to 40 active members), linked by couriers, holding {chargesOutstanding} military shaped charges. No 'Mechs and no formations — just couriers, bombers, and a leadership of 2 to 4 people. The Lattice itself is their greatest asset.
opforSketch.behavior: They never stand, defend, or fight. They bomb symbols of government, time their attacks to the garrison's reactions, and set up situations where the Clan's raw strength looks like brutality on camera. The ceremony attack is the whole point of their campaign; everything before it is setup.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY MAGAZINE
forks.trigger: Network broken and the ceremony held safely.
forks.consequence: Questioning prisoners traces the missing charges to a flooded lower level of the old militia depot outside the city. You must seize the cache intact before the network's successors — or the rival's Watch — reach it first.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN PLAZA
forks.trigger: A bomb goes off inside the ceremony's security zone, or the ceremony is canceled.
forks.consequence: The network delivers the attack it promised, and the city erupts: mourning crowds, revenge mobs attacking police posts, and a garrison that must hold order in the wreckage of its own ceremony.

forks.name: OPERATION TAUGHT WAR
forks.trigger: Three dezgra marks against you, or a mass-casualty accident during the hunt.
forks.consequence: The network levels up. Recruitment triples, the pyramid rebuilds with armed cells in the mining towns, and the garrison spends the next year in a hidden war it taught its own enemy how to fight.

storyElementSeed: An Elemental stands out of his armor at a Lattice tea stall, helmet under one arm, paying for a cup with ration scrip. The stall-keeper's eyes flick to the exits. Both of them pretend this is ordinary.

comstar.objectives.primary: Break the bombing network before the anniversary ceremony. The Blessed Order warns that a power which cannot protect its own registry halls invites every rebel in the occupied zones to draw the same conclusion. Record every step of this hunt; the data itself is holy.

is-liao.decisionPoints[0].context: Nineteen days, one captured courier, and three methods on the table. Someone will report on each one — someone whose loyalty you have not fully bought. Choose the method whose failure you could survive being blamed for.

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no garrison base set up in the capital, so building the grid takes 16 days instead of 12. The network gets those 4 extra days to operate freely.

title: OPERATION SILENT MOORING
skeleton: raider must cut a functioning prize out of a rival's stronghold with a bid too small to win a stand-up fight, where the prize must leave under its own power and the garrison stays honor-barred only while the raid keeps inside its declared terms
inspiration: the cutting-out of HMS Hermione, Puerto Cabello, 1799
situation: {EMPLOYER} and {TARGET_FACTION} share {WORLD}, and sharing is the wound. The rival's base in the Kerensky Caldera holds what your Khan wants flying your Clan's colors: the Vantaa refit line — {prizeMachines} OmniMechs of a new design proven against the Inner Sphere, plus the mobile calibration gantry that lets the design be copied. Your commander won the right to this Trial of Possession — a formal fight over who owns something — in the bidding circle, and won it the Clan way: by promising to attack with fewer and fewer forces until no rival would offer to use less. That promise is now the mission. {FORCE_SIZE}, and not one machine more, against a base whose garrison is a full Cluster. The Trial terms, sealed by both Clans' Loremasters, are the only reason the math is survivable: inside the marked circle, the defenders may field no more force than the attacker bid; garrison forces outside the circle are honor-bound to stay out for 4 hours after the Trial starts; and the circle is drawn around the refit field itself, not the roads leading out. Everything else is the problem. The prize must leave working — a wrecked OmniMech is no prize — and the gantry crawler moves at 32 kilometers per hour, never faster. The caldera has 2 ramp roads. The northern ramp passes 900 meters below a garrison gun battery that sits outside the circle and so cannot be touched — unless it fires first, and whether it will is a question your Watch cannot answer. That report is 4 days old and its read on the battery's orders is only a guess. The prize 'Mechs start powered down, and each takes 12 minutes to start up on a design its new pilot has never flown. So the bid must include warriors who arrive empty-handed and leave flying the captured 'Mechs. {NPC:intel-source} has provided the base's guard schedule and one more thing: the rival's bondsman techs at the line — {bondsmanTechs} of them, captured from a Combine regiment in {YEAR} — have no love for their captors. What they will do when shooting starts is unconfirmed; it rests on a single Watch conversation through a merchant go-between. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the defending Star and has never lost inside a circle. The garrison Cluster waits at the caldera rim for any broken term — a shot fired outside the circle, damage to an undeclared building — that would make the entire base lawfully theirs to keep.

objectives.primary: Get {prizeMachines} refit OmniMechs and the calibration gantry out of the caldera in working order before the Trial terms expire at T+4:00:00.
objectives.secondary: Finish the Trial without breaking any term — no fighting undeclared forces or damaging undeclared buildings.
objectives.bonus: Bring out the bondsman techs who are willing to come; they carry refit knowledge the gantry alone cannot replace.

complications.name: Cold Machines
complications.text: The prize 'Mechs stand powered down, running a design their new pilots have never flown. Each takes 12 minutes to start up once a pilot is in the seat, and the gantry crawler needs 20 minutes to warm up before it can move at all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After a pilot boards, a prize OmniMech cannot move or fire for 4 full turns, then moves at half speed with no weapons for 2 more turns. The gantry cannot move until turn 7 at the earliest.

complications.name: The Overlook Battery
complications.text: The northern ramp runs 900 meters below a garrison gun battery that sits outside the circle. Its orders are unknown, and our read on them is only a guess. If it fires on your column, the terms are already broken — by them. But proving who broke them first is another matter.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When your column enters the battery's firing arc, roll for its stance. Firing back before it attacks you counts as YOU breaking the terms. Taking its first salvo without firing back keeps your claim intact, but costs you armor.

complications.name: The Slow Crawl
complications.text: The gantry moves at 32 kilometers per hour, and the whole column can only go as fast as the gantry. The northern ramp climb takes 40 minutes at that speed; the southern ramp takes 65 minutes but avoids the battery completely.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You choose the route against the clock. North leaves 28 minutes of spare time inside the terms, but you face the battery. South leaves only 3 minutes of spare time, but no battery.

decisionPoints.name: The Shape of the Bid
decisionPoints.context: The size of your bid is fixed, but what goes into it is not. Inside the circle you will fight whatever the defending Star brings, and the prize must still walk out. Cutting the bid won you the Trial — now you have to make it work.

options.title: Load Up on Pilots
advantages: Put 5 pilot-teams and 2 Elemental Points in the bid, so every prize 'Mech has a pilot boarding in the first minutes
You can extract everything at once — 'Mechs, gantry, and techs in one column
Elementals can seize the gantry crew cabin intact without firing a shot
disadvantages: That leaves only 3 OmniMechs to escort, against a full defending Star
If {NPC:opfor-commander} presses the circle fight hard, your escort is spent before the prize 'Mechs even start up
Pilot-teams caught on foot are casualties, not fighters
options.consequence: Everything depends on your escort surviving 6 turns. Win those turns and the Trial is a total success; lose them and this bid is remembered as the one that sent hands where it needed fists.

costs.resource: BID — escort cut to 3 OmniMechs; you fight the circle 3 against 5
costs.risk: Six turns with the prize 'Mechs cold and the enemy unbroken — call it even odds

options.title: Load Up on Fighters
advantages: Put a full Star of OmniMechs in the bid, so you can win the circle fight on merit
{NPC:opfor-commander}'s record says the defense will fight one-on-one duels, and duels favor your veterans
No part of the plan depends on the bondsman techs, whose loyalty is unproven
disadvantages: That leaves only 2 pilot-teams, so at most 2 prize 'Mechs and the gantry come out — partial by design
Three refit OmniMechs are left standing in the rival's field, an obvious loose end
The Loremasters will record a Trial won but a prize only half-taken
options.consequence: You win the circle cleanly and pull out with everything you could carry. When the rival next issues a batchall — a formal challenge — they will name the 3 'Mechs you left as the prize, and your Khan will ask why they were still there to be named.

costs.resource: ISORLA — 3 of the {prizeMachines} prize 'Mechs deliberately left behind; you take only 40 percent of the prize by weight
costs.risk: HONOR — a won Trial with an abandoned prize reads as a bid that was shaped wrong from the start

options.title: Declare Only the Gantry
advantages: Declaring the Trial for the gantry alone pulls the defense in tight around the line and away from the 'Mech park
Anything your force captures in the fighting counts as lawful battlefield spoils, on top of the declared gantry
The smallest declared prize means the rival's counter-bid is smallest too
disadvantages: This is exploiting a loophole in the open: legal, but remembered as lawyer's war
The rival's Loremaster will dispute every 'Mech you claim as spoils, in council, for years
If the defense refuses to pull in tight, the trick nets you the gantry and nothing else
options.consequence: The Trial ends within its exact wording. You come out with 1 to 4 'Mechs as disputed spoils and the gantry cleanly, but your Clan's name gains a black mark that every future challenge against you will cite.

costs.resource: HONOR — a council grievance case that drags on for years; your Loremaster's time is spent like ammunition
costs.risk: If the circle fight scatters, your spoils claims may be cut down to just 1 'Mech

decisionPoints.name: The Overlook
decisionPoints.context: The column is formed and the gantry is rolling. The northern ramp gives you 28 minutes of spare time; the southern ramp gives you 3. The battery above the north road still has not shown its hand. The terms protect it until it fires, but the clock protects nobody.

options.title: Take the North Road and Take the Hit
advantages: The 28-minute cushion can absorb delays the southern route cannot
If the battery fires first, breaking the terms is on them — and the whole base becomes yours to win
Your column's armor can survive one ranging salvo at 900 meters
disadvantages: One salvo into a cold, defenseless prize 'Mech could void the primary objective in a single hit
Taking fire for 40 minutes without firing back is a hard discipline test under real shelling
If any prize 'Mech fires back on reflex, YOU broke the terms
options.consequence: The column climbs under the guns. Whether the battery commander throws away his career on one salvo decides whose Trial this is — and your pilots' trigger discipline decides it again.

costs.resource: TIME — you keep the full 28-minute cushion
costs.risk: One ranging salvo against cold prize armor, weighed against the battery's orders, which we can only guess at

options.title: Take the South Road, Cut It Close
advantages: No battery, no stance roll, no discipline test
If nothing slows you, the terms run out only after your column is already past the rim
Even if you beat the defending Star, it cannot re-form in time to catch you on the longer road
disadvantages: Only 3 minutes of spare time against a 65-minute climb — a single stall drops you into expired terms
After T+4:00:00 the garrison Cluster is legally free, and it is waiting
None of your crews has ever driven the gantry at full load up a steep grade for that long
options.consequence: The southern ramp becomes a 65-minute gamble on machinery. Go on time and the Trial is flawless; throw one track and your column becomes the garrison Cluster's lawful prey.

costs.resource: TIME — you spend all your spare time up front: 3 minutes against a 65-minute climb
costs.risk: If the terms expire mid-ramp, a full Cluster falls on your column — total loss, riding on the gantry holding together

options.title: Send Elementals to the Guns
advantages: Two Points climb the overlook through cover the guns cannot hit, then sit among the crews — the battery cannot fire on your column with boarders aboard
You keep the north road's 28-minute cushion without taking a salvo
Nothing in the terms calls an unarmed approach to an undeclared position an attack
disadvantages: Nothing in the terms allows it, either — if you are caught, the rival Loremaster can argue you broke the terms
Those 2 Points are your escort's entire infantry reserve
If the gun crews resist and an Elemental strikes first, that is you breaking the terms, in plain sight
options.consequence: The guns stay silent and the column passes — and for the next year, two Loremasters argue over what the boarding really was. The ruling comes back as either vindication or a formal grievance with your commander's name on it.

costs.resource: BID — your infantry reserve is detached at the column's most exposed moment
costs.risk: HONOR — a ruling that you broke the terms turns a won Trial into a defeat in council

entries.event: ALARM — the Trial is declared at the circle's edge; the base's guards confirm your bid force is inbound.
The defending Star is active at the refit field. The circle fight opens on the defenders' terms.
Earliest a prize 'Mech can finish starting up, if pilot-teams boarded the moment fighting began.
Earliest the gantry finishes warming up, so the column can form.
Latest you can leave and still make the southern ramp inside the terms. For the northern ramp, latest departure is T+3:20.
The terms expire. The garrison Cluster is legally free to leave the caldera rim.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+4:00:00 from the Trial's start. At that second the honor bar lifts, a full Cluster is 11 minutes from the ramps, and nothing about the Trial protects anyone still inside the caldera.

opforSketch.composition: Inside the circle: a defending Star matched to your bid — front-line OmniMechs, elite pilots, {NPC:opfor-commander} in command. Outside it: a garrison Cluster at the rim (released if the terms are broken or expire) and one overlook battery of 3 to 4 heavy autocannon emplacements with unknown orders.
opforSketch.behavior: The defending Star fights strict zellbrigen — the Clan honor code of one-on-one duels — and will steer those duels toward the 'Mech park to keep your pilot-teams on foot. The garrison watches for any broken term with a Loremaster's eye, arguing the rules in real time. Expect the defense to spend the clock, not lives — time is their best weapon.

forks.name: OPERATION HELD GROUND
forks.trigger: Prize and gantry extracted inside the terms.
forks.consequence: The rival answers lawfully and fast: within 30 days they declare their own Trial against your base's refit field. What you took must now be defended on home ground, against a bid built by warriors who watched yours work.

forks.name: OPERATION ASHES OF THE BID
forks.trigger: The circle is lost, or the column destroyed or abandoned.
forks.consequence: Your pilot-teams captured in the caldera are the rival's bondsmen now, and the rival's scientist caste is picking the refit knowledge out of their heads. The Khan authorizes a rescue before the adoption rites make them truly the rival's.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN CIRCLE
forks.trigger: A ruling that you broke the terms.
forks.consequence: The safcon — the safe-conduct agreement that keeps the two Clans from open war on {WORLD} — is void. Skirmishing breaks out along the whole shared border, and what was a single Trial becomes a war neither Khan ordered.

storyElementSeed: In the dark staging area, a pilot-team warrior sits on an ammunition crate, memorizing an unfamiliar cockpit layout from a hand-drawn card. Her lips move through the startup sequence — twelve minutes she must know by heart before dawn.

is-davion.objectives.secondary: Stay inside the exact wording of the agreement — do not fire on any undeclared force. The whole extraction works only because their own rules keep the Cluster at the rim. Give them one legal excuse, and those rules turn into a Cluster coming for your column.

prizeMachines.unit: refit OmniMechs at the Vantaa line

bondsmanTechs.unit: bondsman technicians at the refit line

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no dropships staged, so the Trial cannot begin this cycle. The Loremaster's seal expires in 60 days and the bidding reopens — probably at a higher bid than yours.

title: OPERATION MEASURED GROUND
skeleton: an expendable rearguard must trade ground on a fixed timetable across successive lines, surviving each stand in order to make the next, while its own members hunt the single decisive death the schedule cannot afford
inspiration: the 316th Rifle Division's delay on the Volokolamsk highway, 1941
situation: The Galaxy is leaving. A counter-offensive 2 jumps coreward has pulled every front-line Cluster off {WORLD}. The replacement Galaxy will land its DropShips at the Tessen corridor at T+264:00 — 11 days from now — but only if the corridor is still held when they commit. Holding it is your job. You command a solahma Cluster: aging warriors, average age 58, riding worn second-line 'Mechs with 30 percent fewer machines fit to fight than the roster shows. The Galaxy commander named you the rearguard and, in the order, called it 'a fitting end' — and meant it as a kindness. The enemy is a Combine counter-attack force, confident after their win at Tukayyid: a veteran combined-arms regiment, led by artillery and backed by 2 aerospace squadrons, advancing up the Tessen Valley at a steady 25 kilometers per day. That report is one day old and reliable. They do not accept duels; they have learned better. The ground is your one advantage. The valley climbs through 4 cliff lines — AMBER, CINDER, FALLOW, and SLATE — each a natural defensive position 15 to 20 kilometers behind the last. West of every line lie the Tessen salt pans, the campaign's terrain problem: by day the crust softens and bogs down anything over 35 tons, but at night it freezes hard enough to carry even assault 'Mechs for {panWindow} hours. So every line holds firmly by day and can be turned from the west between midnight and dawn. The cruelty is in the schedule. It requires you to hold each line until its set date, then give it up cleanly — pull back intact, preserve the force, and man the next line. But solahma doctrine, and 58-year-old hearts, want the opposite: these warriors were given a last command exactly so they could die carrying it out, and every one of them knows that a rearguard which survives its own battle has, by one reading, failed to spend itself properly. {NPC:opfor-commander} knows this and has built the campaign to exploit it — fake openings that look like a chance for glory, single-'Mech challenges shouted over open radio, deliberate insults meant to pull a Star off its line into a kill zone. The first civilian evacuation columns share the corridor road for 3 more days. At T+264:00 the DropShips either land at SLATE or divert elsewhere — and if they divert, the corridor and everyone on it is lost.

objectives.primary: Hold Line SLATE in fighting condition at T+264:00, when the replacement Galaxy's DropShips land at the Tessen corridor.
objectives.secondary: Do not give up AMBER, CINDER, or FALLOW before their set dates (T+72:00, T+144:00, T+216:00). The enemy must take the full 11 days to reach SLATE.
objectives.bonus: Keep 50 percent or more of the Cluster's fighting strength at T+264:00, fit to screen the relief landing.

complications.name: The Salt Pan Clock
complications.text: Each night the pans freeze solid for {panWindow} hours, and heavy forces can then cross them to flank any line. The enemy probes the pans every single night.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During the nightly freeze, the western flank of your line is open ground. Any line you do not bend back or screen to the west during that window can be turned without a frontal attack.

complications.name: Machine Wear
complications.text: The Cluster's worn second-line 'Mechs break down faster the longer they fight, and there is no repair depot behind them to fix the damage.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After each fighting withdrawal, 1 in 4 surviving 'Mechs breaks down and cannot fight — unless the force takes a 12-hour repair pause. The schedule has no room for that pause unless you give up a line early.

complications.name: The Good Death
complications.text: To solahma warriors, a rearguard order sounds like permission to die well. {NPC:opfor-commander} broadcasts single-combat challenges and insults over open radio, hunting for the Star that will break formation to answer with honor.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any Star cut below half strength, or challenged directly over open radio, must pass a command check or commit to an all-out fight right where it stands — off-schedule and with no support.

complications.name: Shared Road
complications.text: Civilian evacuation columns clog the corridor road behind your lines until T+72:00. Demolitions, artillery duels, and your own retreating traffic all fight for the same road.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until T+72:00, your withdrawals move at half speed, and any indirect-fire mission within 2 kilometers of the road needs a clearance step that costs one full turn.

decisionPoints.name: The Price of CINDER
decisionPoints.context: Line CINDER's western anchor collapsed at dawn. A night flanking attack across the pans caught the screening Star just as the crust began to thaw. You can restore the line, give it up, or spend future strength to save it now. The schedule says CINDER should hold 30 more hours; the map says it holds none.

options.title: Counterattack at the Anchor
advantages: The thaw has caught the flanking force on softening crust — counterattack now and their heavy 'Mechs fight at half mobility with a bog at their backs
CINDER is restored to its date, saving both the schedule and the next line's prep time
The Cluster gets the battle it is craving, on ground that favors it
disadvantages: A counterattack spends strength you cannot replace — expect to lose 30 to 40 percent of what remains
Win or lose, the wear from a full battle knocks out a quarter of what is left
Every warrior in the assault will fight it as the good death, so calling them back mid-success may simply fail
options.consequence: CINDER holds to its date over the wrecks of the flanking battalion and a third of your Cluster. The schedule survives whole — but the bonus objective dies here, on the morning the rearguard finally got its battle.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — 30 to 40 percent of remaining Cluster strength committed and not coming back
costs.risk: If the recall fails mid-assault, the counterattack becomes a last stand the schedule cannot absorb

options.title: Give Up CINDER Early, Reinforce FALLOW
advantages: The force breaks contact intact and earns a 12-hour repair pause, resetting the machine wear
FALLOW's prep time doubles, making it the strongest line of the campaign
No warrior is asked to die for a date the map has already overruled
disadvantages: The enemy gains 30 hours and broadcasts it: a Clan line given up ahead of schedule, announced in the open
FALLOW must now hold 102 hours instead of 72 — and it is your weakest position
Giving up a line early once makes doing it again thinkable, which sharpens the discipline problem
options.consequence: The Cluster reaches FALLOW whole and rested, and FALLOW becomes the whole campaign: 4 days of grinding defense against an enemy that arrives early, confident, and on schedule for SLATE if FALLOW cracks.

costs.resource: TIME — 30 hours of schedule given up; FALLOW must now hold for 102 hours
costs.risk: HONOR — a line given up early is recorded in every warrior's codex, and the enemy's broadcasts rub it in nightly

options.title: Mine the Pans by Night
advantages: Your mobile Star mines the northern pan crossings during the freeze window, closing the night flank for the rest of the campaign
With no flank to fear, CINDER's front can be held by daytime gunnery alone
One night's work saves a battle's worth of blood
disadvantages: The mobile Star is your only reserve, and it spends the night out on the pans instead of behind the line
If it is caught on the crust when the thaw comes, the whole Star is lost — 'Mechs bogged to the hip under enemy artillery
Your mines cover 2 of the 3 usable crossing lanes; the third stays open and you must guess which one it is
options.consequence: Two lanes close for good. The campaign now hinges on whether the enemy's night probes find the third lane before SLATE — and on a reserve Star that spent its safety margin hauling mines across a freezing sea.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — your entire mine stock and the reserve Star's whole night are committed; no reserve behind CINDER until dawn
costs.risk: Misjudge the thaw and the Star is stranded on the pans — the whole reserve lost, riding on a 2-hour margin

entries.event: ALARM — the enemy vanguard makes contact at Line AMBER; the delay campaign clock starts.
AMBER's set yield date. Civilian columns clear the corridor road; demolition restrictions lift.
CINDER's set yield date.
FALLOW's set yield date. SLATE must be fully occupied by now.
The replacement Galaxy's DropShips begin their landing burns — they will commit or divert based on the corridor's status.
The DropShips land at the Tessen corridor behind Line SLATE.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+264:00. If SLATE is not held in fighting condition at that hour, the DropShips divert to the other continent, the corridor is lost, and the Cluster's last command ends 15 kilometers short of mattering.

opforSketch.composition: Combine combined-arms regiment, veteran: 2 'Mech battalions (fast heavies forward), 1 armor battalion, self-propelled artillery battalion, 2 aerospace squadrons flying interdiction. Logistics-rich and unhurried.
opforSketch.behavior: A deliberate advance — 25 kilometers per day, artillery softening before every contact, no duels accepted. It probes the salt pans every freeze window. It uses open-radio challenges and calculated insults as weapons aimed at solahma discipline, and hides a kill zone behind every fake opening.

forks.name: OPERATION TURNED BLADE
forks.trigger: SLATE held at T+264:00 with the relief landed.
forks.consequence: The replacement Galaxy strikes down the valley from the secured landing grounds, using the solahma survivors as guides and screen. This is the counterattack their 11 days bought — and a second chapter to their last command.

forks.name: OPERATION GLEANED IRON
forks.trigger: SLATE held, but Cluster strength fell below the level needed to screen the landing.
forks.consequence: The relief lands into a corridor held by wrecks and walking wounded. Its first job is not the counterattack but a rescue: fighting its way out to the shattered Stars still holding hillsides nobody ordered them to leave.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD FURROWS
forks.trigger: SLATE falls or the DropShips divert.
forks.consequence: The corridor is lost. The Cluster's survivors — too slow to outrun the advance, too proud to surrender to it — hide in the cliff country to make the occupation pay for every day it stays. A solahma guerrilla war is its own kind of ending.

storyElementSeed: At a FALLOW gun position, an old warrior repaints a faded kill tally on a borrowed 'Mech's shin by lantern light. Then he adds the names of the next two lines below it, with their dates — like appointments he means to keep.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: Hold Line SLATE through T+264:00 so the relief force lands behind a living shield. The Combine force facing you has waited 300 years for this revenge. Your duty is to make them spend the full 11 days taking it — not to throw your lives away cheaply.

panWindow.unit: hours of load-bearing freeze per night

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no engineering depot in the corridor, so your mines cover only 1 crossing lane instead of 2. This option then closes just a third of the night flank.

title: OPERATION STANDING SMOKE
skeleton: a beaten force must lift everything that defines it off a hostile shore on an externally enforced timetable without ever appearing to retreat, while watchers wait for the moment thinning lines make the remainder lawful prize
inspiration: the evacuation of Gallipoli, December 1915 - January 1916
situation: The battle of Tukayyid set more than a truce line. The Council ruling that followed orders {EMPLOYER} to leave {WORLD} — a world now on the wrong side of the agreed border — within 30 days, watched over by ComStar. Their Precentor keeps a safe-passage corridor open exactly that long and not one hour more. You must lift out everything that marks a Clan's presence here: 2 Trinaries of equipment, the base's stores of war-spoils, {bondsmenCount} bondsmen (captives taken into Clan service), 140 wounded, and — above all other cargo — the genetic legacy shipment: 6 cryo-cradles that need constant refrigeration power and travel under a sacred-cargo guard. The hard part is not the lifting. It is not being seen to leave. A Clan that retreats becomes prey; a Clan that withdraws in contempt is simply elsewhere. So the garrison must look full-strength until the final hour, because 3 audiences are watching for the moment it does not. First: the planetary resistance, whose probing attacks have doubled since the ruling became known (that report is 2 days old and reliable). Second: an Inner Sphere advance party due to land on day 25 to take over the government. And third, the one that matters most: a Star of {TARGET_FACTION}, landed under observer rights, waiting beside their DropShip for the instant Clan law lets them claim any abandoned equipment as lawful prize. Under Clan law, gear left unguarded at a withdrawal is exactly that. Your tools for the deception are limited: {dronePosts} automated sentry posts that fake patrol movement, radio decoys that fake Trinary comm nets, and the foundry smokestacks, kept burning by a skeleton crew so the skyline never changes. Every Star you lift out widens the gap the automation must cover. The terrain problem is the Vellamo landing field: the base's only hardened field sits on a river terrace below the city bluffs, and every approach to it is visible from 11 kilometers away in daylight. Loading can only stay hidden in the 9-hour river fog that fills the terrace from about midnight to mid-morning. {NPC:intel-source} reports the resistance has moved a captured artillery battery within range of the field, but its exact position is unconfirmed — we know only from sound-ranging. The Precentor's corridor closes at T+720:00. Anything not aboard a DropShip by that hour can be lawfully seized — claimed by the rival Clan, taken by the resistance, or handed to the incoming Inner Sphere government.

objectives.primary: Lift the genetic legacy shipment, the wounded, and both Trinaries of equipment out through the Vellamo field before the corridor closes at T+720:00.
objectives.secondary: Keep the garrison looking full-strength until T+696:00 — no watcher should realize the base is emptying before the final day.
objectives.bonus: Lift out all {bondsmenCount} bondsmen and the war-spoils stores — leave nothing behind to be claimed as prize or used to arm the resistance.

complications.name: The Thinning Line
complications.text: Every Star you lift out hands its patrol sector to automation. Each drone post covers 400 meters and fails at a steady rate, and the resistance maps every gap within a day.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The more of your force you have lifted, the more often the resistance raids: one probe every 72 hours below 30 percent lifted, one every 24 hours above 60 percent. Each failed drone post leaves a permanent gap until someone resets it by hand.

complications.name: Sacred Cargo
complications.text: The 6 legacy cradles need constant refrigeration power and a warrior guard by ritual. They can move to the field only once, only during the night fog, and cannot sit on the ground more than 20 hours on portable power.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Moving the legacy is a single all-in convoy run inside one fog window. Once it starts it cannot be called back, and its guard (1 full Star) is pulled out of the garrison's visible strength for that night.

complications.name: The Watching Rival Clan
complications.text: The {TARGET_FACTION} observer Star keeps testing the edges of your withdrawal — a sensor sweep here, a walked perimeter there — building a case that you have already legally abandoned the site.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any equipment park left with no live warrior guard for 6 hours straight becomes claimable, and the observers will notice within 2 hours. Once they declare a claim, you can only answer it by giving in or by fighting a Trial.

complications.name: The Hidden Artillery
complications.text: The captured battery is real, but its position is unconfirmed — we only know it from sound-ranging. If it shells a loading operation in the fog, firing back means dropping shells into civilian neighborhoods on a world you are handing over in 3 weeks.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The battery's first fire mission lands on a field operation of the GM's choosing. Firing back destroys the battery but trips the political condition of the COMPROMISED outcome; taking the hit without answering costs you the operation underway.

decisionPoints.name: What the Last Ships Carry
decisionPoints.context: On day 22 a lifting DropShip is knocked out by ground fire to a drive nozzle — repairs will take 8 days, 2 days past the corridor's close. The remaining ships can lift only 84 percent of what is left. You must leave 16 percent of a Clan behind, and other Clans will read your choice as a statement of your values.

options.title: Leave the Machines, Take the People
advantages: The legacies, the wounded, and the bondsmen all lift out — no life and no bloodline left behind
The human half of the bonus objective survives
No warrior has to guard an empty equipment park against a claim you cannot fight
disadvantages: Two Stars of OmniMechs and the war-spoils stores stay on the field — lawful prize the observer Star will claim within hours
Whatever the observers do not want, the armed resistance inherits
A Clan that buys back its people by giving up its machines will hear about both forever
options.consequence: The rival's claim is declared before the last ship clears the sky, and your Clan's machines wear another Clan's paint by season's end — a fact thrown in your officers' faces at every bidding circle for years.

costs.resource: ISORLA — 2 Stars of equipment and all war-spoils stores lost to the claim; the prize ledger runs against your Clan
costs.risk: HONOR — the observer Star's Loremaster files the abandonment as a precedent with the Grand Council

options.title: Take the Machines, Leave the People
advantages: All the fighting equipment lifts out — the Clan's strength stays whole
No prize claim is possible; the observers go home empty-handed
The wounded who can fight again travel with their machines
disadvantages: {bondsmenCount} bondsmen and 40 of the worst wounded are left for the Inner Sphere government — and abandoned bondsmen become the Inner Sphere's best-informed spies
Leaving the wounded behind is read aloud in council by every enemy your Khan has
The legacy guard must be thinned to cover the extra equipment lift, halving the sacred cargo's safety margin
options.consequence: The equipment lifts and the people stay. Within a year, the questioned bondsmen have given the Inner Sphere the base's order of battle, its refit procedures, and the name of every officer who voted to leave them.

costs.resource: HONOR — wounded and bondsmen abandoned to the enemy; the codex entry writes itself and is never erased
costs.risk: A huge intelligence loss — the enemy gains the base's complete technical and organizational picture

options.title: Hold Past the Corridor
advantages: Eight days of repair lets you lift everything — equipment, people, legacies, stores — a complete withdrawal
No claim, no abandonment, no hard choices; the whole cargo problem simply goes away
The garrison looks full-strength because it actually is
disadvantages: The Precentor's corridor closes at T+720:00 with no appeal; after that, the safe-passage and the local truce protections end
The Inner Sphere government's fleet arrives with a naval escort on day 25 — and an armed Clan base with no legal right to be there meets it on day 30
ComStar records the violation against your Clan in the truce ledger, to be collected whenever they choose
options.consequence: The repair finishes in 7 days or it does not. Either the last ships lift out through a closing net with everything aboard, or the base fights the exact battle the truce was signed to prevent, on ground already given away.

costs.resource: TIME — 2 days past the corridor's close, with no safe-passage, against an arriving naval escort
costs.risk: ComStar files a truce violation against the Clan — a strategic debt with no stated price

decisionPoints.name: What to Do With the Leftovers
decisionPoints.context: Whatever you cannot lift out must be dealt with before the last fog window. The observer Star sits parked within sight of the equipment grounds, waiting. You have three choices, and each sends a message every Clan will read.

options.title: Give Them Away Formally
advantages: A formal gift turns a humiliating claim into a choice you made — and that difference matters in council
Nothing reaches the resistance; the rival Clan guards what you give them
The rival owes you a recorded debt of equipment, which you can call in during future bidding
disadvantages: You strengthen a rival Clan with your own equipment, by your own hand
A gift made under pressure fools no Loremaster, whatever the record says
Your own warriors watch their machines handed over washed and fueled
options.consequence: The gift is accepted with proper ceremony and remembered without it. The rival's gratitude lasts until the next bidding circle; the equipment lasts a good deal longer.

costs.resource: ISORLA — the leftovers transfer whole to a rival Clan, logged as a gift
costs.risk: HONOR — council reads the ceremony; everyone else reads the pressure behind it

options.title: Destroy Them on the Field
advantages: Nothing goes to the rival Clan, the resistance, or the incoming government
Demolition is fast, sure, and needs no negotiation with anyone
The message — a Clan destroys what it cannot keep — carries its own cold dignity
disadvantages: Deliberately wasting war materiel insults everything the caste system exists to conserve
The demolition costs 2 days of engineer time the lift schedule can barely spare
Columns of smoke over the equipment grounds announce your withdrawal to all 3 audiences at once
options.consequence: The leftovers burn for 2 days, visible from orbit. Your full-strength cover story dies with them — and the final lift operations run against a resistance that no longer has to guess you are leaving.

costs.resource: TIME — 2 days of engineer work and the last of your cover story, spent together
costs.risk: The secondary objective fails the moment the first charge goes off; the final fog windows run at maximum raid tempo

options.title: Hand Them to ComStar
advantages: Letting ComStar rule on the leftovers cancels the observer Star's one-sided claim
In ComStar's keeping, the equipment is safe from the resistance until the government arrives
No Clan hand makes the surrender; the paperwork does
disadvantages: Asking ComStar to rule on Clan property is a precedent the Council will hate — one more inch given away
The arbitration takes 4 days the schedule can barely hold
The ruling may award the rival everything anyway, now with an official stamp on it
options.consequence: The Precentor accepts custody, clearly pleased. The equipment question closes cleanly, but the precedent — a Clan asking ComStar to hold its goods — opens a longer account in the Council's memory.

costs.resource: HONOR — the precedent of ComStar holding Clan property, filed under your commander's name
costs.risk: The arbitration may still award the rival the equipment — now with legitimacy attached

entries.event: ALARM — the first company-strength resistance probe hits the landing field's perimeter; they have read the Council ruling.
The first equipment Trinary is lifted out. Automation now covers 25 percent of the patrol sectors.
Crisis point: you must decide what to cut after the DropShip is knocked out, or the rest of the schedule cannot close.
The Inner Sphere government's advance party lands at the other field (day 25), with a naval escort in orbit.
The final fog window opens. The legacy convoy and last lift operations happen inside it or not at all.
The ComStar corridor closes.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hard deadline T+720:00 (30 days). At that hour the ComStar Precentor closes the safe-passage corridor under the Council ruling, with no appeal. Anything still on {WORLD} after that loses its protection: it is no longer covered by the truce or by Clan law, which means the rival observer Star, the resistance, or the incoming Inner Sphere government can lawfully claim it.

opforSketch.composition: Three separate, uncoordinated threats: a planetary resistance of about a battalion of infantry with technicals, mines, and 1 captured artillery battery (position unconfirmed); a {TARGET_FACTION} observer Star (front-line, elite, but legally limited); and an Inner Sphere government advance party with a corvette escort arriving day 25. None work together, but all benefit from the same failures.
opforSketch.behavior: The resistance probes wherever automation replaces live troops, and saves its battery for one field operation. The observer Star fights nothing and watches everything, arguing in real time that you have abandoned the site. The Inner Sphere party wants a quiet handover and will not fight unless the corridor lapses — after which it must.

forks.name: OPERATION SETTLED ACCOUNT
forks.trigger: All primary cargo lifted inside the corridor with the cover story held.
forks.consequence: The withdrawal reads as contempt, not defeat. The lifted Trinaries redeploy to the new border garrison — where the same resistance networks, carried over by the handover, begin testing the line through its first winter.

forks.name: OPERATION RECLAIMED LINEAGE
forks.trigger: The legacy shipment is lost, grounded past the deadline, or captured.
forks.consequence: Six cryo-cradles of the Clan's bloodlines are in resistance hands, being offered through brokers to an Inner Sphere genetics lab. The Khan's order is one line: recover them before the lab starts experimenting on them.

forks.name: OPERATION ANSWERED INSULT
forks.trigger: Firing back into civilian districts, staying past the corridor, or giving up a claim under protest.
forks.consequence: The Council demands the shame be answered. Your unit is ordered to strike a formal, sanctioned blow against the rival that profited — a Trial with the whole Clan's honor riding on a single battle.

storyElementSeed: At dusk a technician walks the empty barracks rows, switching on lamps in the windows one by one to a written schedule, so the city below sees a garrison sitting down to its evening meal.

comstar.objectives.secondary: Keep the garrison looking full-strength until T+696:00. The Blessed Order's corridor exists to make this withdrawal orderly. What the Clans call honor, the Order calls staying on schedule — and the same discipline serves both.

resourceGates.lackingText: No Clan JumpShip stays in the system past the corridor's close. Without your own jump ship, staying longer is not an option — you must decide what to cut from the knocked-out DropShip's cargo.

title: OPERATION OPEN HAND
skeleton: a collector must assemble proof of a rival's hidden strength that can be openly avowed before a fixed tribunal date, while every covert shortcut would convert the accuser into the accused and the surest sensor is a challenge that must then be fought
inspiration: U-2 imagery and the UN Security Council presentation, Cuba, 1962
situation: The border between the {EMPLOYER} and {TARGET_FACTION} zones on {WORLD} was set by agreement and kept by numbers: each Clan told the other's Loremaster exactly how large its garrison is, and those honest declarations are the peace. Your Watch believes the rival lied. The evidence so far is only circumstantial: the Krath foundry in {DISTRICT} draws a third more power than its declared work needs, grain orders feed {hiddenWarriors} more mouths than the rolls admit, and there were 2 nighttime sightings of OmniMech road convoys heading toward the foundry's slag field. Those convoy sightings are 11 days old and shaky. The Watch's read: an undeclared second-line Cluster, hidden underground in the old mine tunnels beneath the foundry, cycling below the surface on a 31-hour schedule timed to satellite passes. Your Khan intends to make the accusation at the Grand Council session at T+312:00 — 13 days out — where the Loremaster will demand the rival forfeit the border district as the penalty. The mission is to get the proof, and the proof has rules. An accusation in council must be avowed — sworn to. Every fact you present must have a named source your Loremaster can defend against open challenge.
