A skulker's evidence — from a Watch agent caught sneaking around a rival base — does worse than fail: it turns the accuser into the accused, forces your Khan into surkai (a ritual apology) before all the assembled Clans, and hands the rival a formal grievance blessed by the Council. The terrain problem is the Krath slag field itself: 60 square kilometers of foundry waste, still hot and magnetically noisy, where the rival dumps molten slag on a schedule that — by design or by luck — floods every long-range sensor with interference. Honest instruments go blind exactly where the lie is hidden. There is one 'sensor' the rules cannot blind: the batchall — the formal combat challenge. Declaring a Trial for any border asset forces the defender to declare what forces they have to defend it. A defender hiding a Cluster must then either reveal it in the bid or lie in front of witnesses. The catch: once you declare a Trial, you must fight it, win or lose — so choose a prize small enough that it is not worth either side's blood. {NPC:intel-source} adds a warning: a Crusader faction on your own Galaxy staff sees the border agreement as weakness and this accusation as a distraction. Anything shown at the staff briefing likely reaches the rival within 48 hours. It is unconfirmed, but one earlier leak was traced and never punished.

objectives.primary: Deliver sworn proof of the hidden Cluster to the Loremaster by T+288:00 for authentication — proof with a named source you can defend in open council.
objectives.secondary: Get the proof without doing anything the rival can paint as spying or as breaking the border agreement.
objectives.bonus: Pin down the hidden Cluster's exact size and makeup, so the forfeit demand in council can be sized to match it.

complications.name: The Slag Field
complications.text: Scheduled dumping of molten slag floods the sensors — heat, magnetism, and ground vibration — all along the approach to the foundry tunnels. The interference looks exactly like deliberate hiding and also like ordinary industry, which is the rival's whole defense.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All long-range sensing into {DISTRICT} takes two penalty steps. Readings taken during the 6-hour gap between dumps take none — but the rival controls when that gap happens.

complications.name: The Sworn-Proof Rule
complications.text: Every fact in the council brief needs a named, defensible source: a warrior swearing to what they saw from lawful ground, an instrument record from your own zone, or a merchant's shipping record from open trade. Anything else poisons the whole brief.
complications.mechanicalEffect: As you gather it, each piece of evidence is marked either SWORN (clean) or TAINTED (spy-gathered). One TAINTED item in the final brief voids the accusation and trips the COMPROMISED outcome. The brief's strength equals the number of SWORN items; you need 4 for a council ruling.

complications.name: The Leak on Your Own Staff
complications.text: Any plan shown to the Galaxy staff reaches the rival within 48 hours. The Watch cannot yet prove which officer is leaking.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any collection effort that appears in a staff briefing is countered by the rival 48 hours later — sensor gaps close, convoys stop, the 31-hour rotation reshuffles. Running an effort without briefing it avoids that, but risks an insubordination charge if it fails.

complications.name: The Deadline Has No Appeal
complications.text: The Grand Council session meets at T+312:00. The Loremaster needs the evidence in hand 24 hours before that to authenticate it. An accusation made without proof, or withdrawn, costs the Khan standing that took a decade to build.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The mission is graded at T+288:00 exactly. Evidence that arrives later is worth nothing, no matter how good it is.

decisionPoints.name: How to Get the Proof
decisionPoints.context: Thirteen days, three legal methods, and resources to fully back only one of them. The Loremaster's guidance is typically brief: bring proof you can swear to, and bring it complete.

options.title: The Patient Survey
advantages: Gravity and ground-vibration sensors on your own side of the line, run by sworn warrior-technicians — a source no one can question
Over 10 days, the occupied mine tunnels show up in the buildup of readings that no slag dump can fully hide
Nothing about it can be called spying; the instruments never leave your zone
disadvantages: Ten days of collection against a 13-day deadline leaves no room to re-do a single disputed reading
Circumstantial evidence, even sworn, is the weakest kind of proof — the council may call it merely suggestive and refuse the forfeit
If the rival is warned, they can stretch the dump schedule until your collection runs out of usefulness
options.consequence: The sensors deliver 3 SWORN items of matching circumstantial evidence by T+264:00. Whether 3 sworn inferences outweigh 1 missing photograph is decided by minds in the council chamber your Loremaster cannot control.

costs.resource: TIME — your entire margin; a disputed reading cannot be re-run
costs.risk: The council may grade matching circumstantial evidence below the 4-item bar, and the accusation lands weak

options.title: The Revealing Challenge
advantages: Declaring a Trial for the border relay station forces the rival to declare their defending forces in front of witnesses
An honest bid exposes the hidden Cluster outright; a false bid, later disproven, is a worse council offense than the garrison lie itself
The challenge record is the strongest source there is — the rival's own words
disadvantages: You must then fight the Trial: a Star committed against whatever they bid, for a relay your Clan does not even want
A defender who smells the trick bids small, fights with only declared forces, and proves nothing
Win or lose, you spend blood on an evidence trick — and the Crusader faction will call it playing games with warriors' lives
options.consequence: The challenge goes out and the answer becomes the mission: either the rival's bid betrays the hidden Cluster and your council case is made in their own words, or your Star fights a real Trial for a worthless relay and you have no proof at all.

costs.resource: BID — one Star committed to a Trial fought for evidence, not gain; casualties are the price of admission
costs.risk: HONOR — if they see through the trick, your codex records a Trial declared for a prize your own Clan scorned

options.title: The Open Caravan
advantages: Merchant-caste trade rights through {DISTRICT} are protected by the agreement, so a grain-and-coolant caravan with Watch-trained merchant observers can ride the foundry road legally
Eyes on the ground inside the district: mine headframes, mess-hall food quantities, convoy ruts — sworn merchant testimony counts as proof
The 8-day round trip fits the deadline with room for one repeat pass
disadvantages: Merchants are not warriors, and a skilled Loremaster can crack their testimony under hostile council challenge
If any observer is caught with tools a trader would not carry, the leap to a spying charge is one council argument away
The rival's customs Star searches caravans on a whim — and finding Watch training, even with no tools, taints everything
options.consequence: The caravan returns with sworn ground truth — headframe counts, ration quantities, a convoy log — 4 SWORN items of honest weight, carried by witnesses whose nerve under council challenge has never been tested before the day it must hold.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — the Watch's merchant network in {DISTRICT} is exposed to customs scrutiny and burned for years if searched
costs.risk: One discovered tool turns the entire brief TAINTED and the accuser into the accused

entries.event: ALARM — the rival's counterintelligence sweep burns a Watch listening post on the border; they know collection has begun.
Anything shown to the Galaxy staff at mission start is now being countered in the field.
The rival Watch has flooded the border corridor; easy collection windows are now closed.
Last practical hour to start moving evidence for authentication.
The Loremaster's authentication deadline. The brief is now whatever it is.
The Grand Council session meets; the accusation is made or dropped.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+288:00. Evidence not in the Loremaster's hands by that hour does not exist as far as the council is concerned, and the accusation goes forward with no proof — or not at all.

opforSketch.composition: Rival Clan border garrison: 1 declared Trinary at the foundry approaches, plus rival Watch counterintelligence teams (4 to 6, vehicle-mounted, heavy on electronics). The suspected hidden Cluster — second-line, {hiddenWarriors} warriors — is the objective, not the opponent: if it ever deploys in the open, the mission has already succeeded.
opforSketch.behavior: Legal and watchful: customs searches, counter-sensor sweeps, changing the slag schedule, and staged provocations near the line meant to lure your collectors one step across it. They want to catch a spy far more than they want to keep the secret.

forks.name: OPERATION COLLECTED DEBT
forks.trigger: The council rules for the accusation; the border district is forfeited to your Clan.
forks.consequence: Now you have to take possession: a district of bitter foundry workers and a departing rival garrison stripping whatever it can carry. Occupying a won argument turns out to be a whole mission of its own.

forks.name: OPERATION PAID FORFEIT
forks.trigger: The brief falls short, or the accusation is withdrawn.
forks.consequence: The rival answers the insult with sanctioned inspection-raids on your own declared facilities, daring you to be caught cheating the way you accused them of cheating. Your installations must survive being inspected.

forks.name: OPERATION BOUGHT SILENCE
forks.trigger: A collector caught on rival ground, or a TAINTED brief exposed in council.
forks.consequence: Your Khan performs surkai — the ritual apology — before the Council, while the rival holds your captured Watch team for questioning. The Khan's private order follows: bring them home before what they know is sworn into the rival's record.

storyElementSeed: Alone in a grain trailer, a merchant observer practices her sworn testimony, reciting headframe counts to the rhythm of the road joints — because in 13 days a Loremaster will try to make her doubt her own eyes.

is-liao.decisionPoints[0].context: Thirteen days to prove a neighbor's garrison is a lie, using only methods that hold up under hostile inspection — because the first rule of accusation is that the accuser gets searched twice. Choose the method whose failure you could disown.

hiddenWarriors.unit: undeclared warriors assessed in the mine galleries

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no instrument depot in the zone, so the gravity sensors must be shipped from the homeworld caches — 6 days in transit. That leaves only a 4-day collection window, which yields 2 SWORN items at best.

title: OPERATION SHORT LEASH
skeleton: a hunter must finish a raider band that bases beyond a line the hunter may not cross, while every pursuit to the line feeds a neighbor's ledger of grievances and the raids are timed to exploit exactly that hesitation
situation: Nine raids in 60 days, and the pattern is not desperation — it is careful study. The band hitting the {EMPLOYER} zone's outer settlements on {WORLD} strikes supply columns and caste depots within 90 minutes of a patrol rotation, every time, then withdraws east across the Hagar Trench into the {TARGET_FACTION} occupation zone, every time. The trench is the terrain problem: a rift cliff running 400 kilometers north to south, which ground forces can descend at exactly 6 graded cuts, all logged by the neighbor's border watch. The band crosses anywhere it likes — it moves on {banditVTOLs} ultralight VTOLs and stripped-down light 'Mechs that rappel down the rift wall at preset anchor points your patrols keep finding a day too late. The band is something the Clans created and will not name: {banditStrength} fighters — Inner Sphere deserters, displaced militia, and 2 confirmed washout warriors from a sibko your own Clan culled — under a leader your Watch knows only by the callsign the victims report, {NPC:opfor-commander}. They hold {abductedLaborers} kidnapped laborer-caste workers at their base, worked as camp labor and paraded as human shields when the band is threatened. That report is 5 days old and only fairly reliable. The trap is political. The neighbor Khan has refused you pursuit rights twice, each time citing your zone's disorder as proof you are unfit to hold it. Their border watch logs every sensor contact within 10 kilometers of the trench, building a grievance case against you line by line — and 3 of your own pursuit feints are already in it. Meanwhile the quarterly supply surge begins in 16 days: 40 convoys on fixed schedules that cannot change. If the band is still active when it starts, every column needs a double escort you cannot provide without stripping the garrison Stars down to nothing. And the worst part: the band's quartermaster buys fuel cells and reaction-mass filters somewhere inside YOUR zone. Two merchant settlements are under Watch suspicion, but the proof is unconfirmed — only serial-numbered filter casings recovered at a raid site. The rot is at home even if the den is not. {NPC:intel-source} can keep the Watch file open 16 more days. After that, the convoy schedule decides for everyone.

objectives.primary: Break the band as a fighting force — leader captured or dead, the VTOLs destroyed — before the quarterly convoy surge begins at T+384:00.
objectives.bonus: Cut off the band's home supply line: identify the merchant settlement supplying them, with proof strong enough to hold up before a caste tribunal.

complications.name: The Grievance Ledger Across the Trench
complications.text: The neighbor's border watch logs every contact near the rift. Each event that looks like a border crossing — a feint, a sensor spike, a pursuit pushed too far — is one more line in a formal grievance being built against your Clan.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A visible crossing tally starts at 3. Each pursuit or operation within 10 kilometers of the trench adds 1 on a failed discipline check. At 7, the neighbor files the grievance: the COMPROMISED outcome arms no matter how the hunt goes.

complications.name: Human Shields
complications.text: The band breaks off the moment a fight passes 8 minutes, and any attack that threatens its base or escape route puts kidnapped laborers on the vehicles in plain view as shields.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Band units automatically disengage after 8 minutes of sustained contact. Any fire mission against a retreating band element risks killing laborers; each laborer death chips away at the secondary objective and costs one population-cooperation step across the whole zone.

complications.name: The Schedule Leak
complications.text: Nine raids timed to patrol rotations is not luck. Either the band watches you brilliantly, or your patrol schedule is leaking from a garrison office to the band's quartermaster along with the fuel filters.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any operation planned through normal garrison staff may be anticipated by the band on a roll. An operation planned inside a sealed command cell is not, but it loses the garrison's coordination support.

decisionPoints.name: The Border Problem
decisionPoints.context: The den is across the trench; the law is on this side of it. Sixteen days. The Galaxy commander's only guidance: the convoys will run on schedule, and the grievance tally will not reach seven. Solve it inside those limits.

options.title: Ask for Joint Hunt Rights
advantages: A joint operation with the neighbor's border Trinary turns the trench into a wall instead of a door
It is legal on every line of the ledger, so the grievance case dries up
The neighbor's own records of the band's crossings become your targeting data
disadvantages: The courier trip and the negotiation eat 9 of your 16 days before a single launch order
The price is on the record: a share of the spoils and captives to the neighbor, plus a formal admission that you could not police your own zone
Everything shared with a joint command travels through the neighbor's staff — and maybe out of it
options.consequence: Rights arrive on day 9 with strings attached. The hunt that follows is short, legal, and shared — and your codex shows forever that the band died with the neighbor's permission, at the neighbor's price.

costs.resource: ISORLA — an agreed share of all band salvage and captives goes to the neighbor; HONOR — asking is itself the admission
costs.risk: If negotiations run even one cycle long, you have only 7 days of operating margin left

options.title: The Tethered Goat
advantages: A decoy convoy on the published surge schedule — Elemental Points hidden in the cargo beds, a ready Star just over the horizon — makes the band attack inside YOUR zone
No trench, no ledger, no neighbor: the fight happens on legal ground at a time you chose
An 8-minute battle is winnable when the ambusher is the one being ambushed
disadvantages: The schedule leak cuts both ways: if the schedule travels, the band knows which convoy is bait
Waiting costs raids — expect 2 to 3 real strikes elsewhere while the trap sits idle
If the band brings the laborers forward as shields once contact opens, the trap must choose in seconds what a tribunal will judge for years
options.consequence: The band either takes the bait and dies by the 8th minute, or smells the trap and feeds elsewhere while your Star and 2 Points sit tied up for a week. The leak decides which — find it first.

costs.resource: BID RESOURCES — a Star plus 2 Elemental Points tied down for up to 7 days; meanwhile 2 to 3 settlements take raids with no screen
costs.risk: If the trap is leaked, the decoy crews become the band's tenth raid

options.title: Cross at Night Without Permission
advantages: The den's location is a fair guess; a one-night rappel assault by 3 Elemental Points ends the band where it sleeps
Done clean and fast, the neighbor's watch logs it as a weather false-alarm and the ledger gains nothing it can prove
You free the laborers at the source instead of pulling them off a moving vehicle
disadvantages: If anything is caught — a downed Elemental, a crashed VTOL, one prisoner — the grievance files itself, now with physical proof attached
Crossing without permission is lawbreaking your Khan must then admit or deny; if he denies it, the assault force officially never existed
The base intelligence is 5 days old: if the band moved camps, the strike hits a camp full of laborers first
options.consequence: One night settles the hunt or convicts the Clan. The Points go down the wall with no recall, no support, and a cover story that only holds if everything goes perfectly.

costs.resource: HONOR — the Khan's ability to deny it is spent the moment boots touch the far wall, and only total success wins it back
costs.risk: Any evidence left across the trench arms the COMPROMISED outcome, with the neighbor holding the proof

entries.event: ALARM — tenth raid: the Kellon caste depot burns; band elements withdraw east toward the trench.
The ready Star launches; the pursuit window opens against a 3-hour band head start.
The band reaches its rift anchor points; ground pursuit ends at the trench edge — or in the ledger.
The trail goes cold. Every option now runs on planning time, not pursuit time.
Latest practical launch for any option that still needs negotiation or trap setup.
The quarterly convoy surge begins: 40 columns on fixed schedules.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hard deadline T+384:00 (16 days). When the quarterly convoy surge begins, the hunt is over whether or not the band is dead: every Star reverts to convoy-escort duty, leaving no force free to chase. The band then raids a fixed, predictable schedule at will, and failing to finish it before the deadline is logged against your unit.

opforSketch.composition: Raider band: {banditStrength} fighters with 8 to 12 stripped light 'Mechs and fast vehicles, plus {banditVTOLs} ultralight VTOLs. Quality is mixed — green riders around a veteran core, including 2 Clan washouts who know your doctrine from the inside. Their base is across the trench; their supply roots run inside your own zone.
opforSketch.behavior: Raid and fade against soft logistics only; they break off after 8 minutes; they push human shields forward when pressed. {NPC:opfor-commander} times every strike to your patrol rotations and treats the trench not as terrain but as a legal shield — their real fortification is your restraint.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN MANIFEST
forks.trigger: Band broken and laborers recovered before the surge.
forks.consequence: The captured quartermaster's records name the merchant settlement that supplied the band — and 2 garrison clerks alongside it. The tribunal wants them arrested quietly, before the convoy season starts and the suppliers slip away in the noise.

forks.name: OPERATION DOUBLED WATCH
forks.trigger: The band still active when the surge begins.
forks.consequence: Forty convoys, only 16 units able to escort them, and a band that knows the schedule. The season becomes a grinding escort campaign where every column is a gamble, paid for in worn-down readiness.

forks.name: OPERATION MEASURED INSULT
forks.trigger: The grievance tally reaches seven, or evidence of an unauthorized crossing.
forks.consequence: The neighbor's grievance succeeds: a Council ruling grants their watch patrol rights in a 40-kilometer strip of YOUR zone. The garrison must now keep order — and save face — under a rival's daily, lawful, maddening watch.

storyElementSeed: A patrol finds a rappel anchor bolted into the rift wall, worn by a season of use, its maintenance tag filled out in the neat hand of someone trained to Clan standard. Nobody on the patrol says the obvious thing aloud.

merc.objectives.primary: Break the band before the convoy season starts. The contract pays for convoy losses avoided, not for kills — but understand the employer's politics: chase the band across that trench line and you become the very incident the neighbor is looking for.

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no forward base near the outer settlements, so the over-the-horizon ready Star has to stage from the zone capital. Reaction time triples, and the 8-minute battle turns into a 25-minute pursuit the band wins.

title: OPERATION PAPER DIKE
skeleton: a native auxiliary must end its own people's uprising inside a patron's patience window, knowing that both failure and a call for help end with the patron's war machines doing the work on the patron's terms
inspiration: the workers' uprising in East Berlin and the Soviet intervention, 17 June 1953
situation: The occupier lets {WORLD} keep a civil watch: 2,300 constables and the Home District Armored Section — {militiaVehicles} wheeled armored cars and 2 unarmed IndustrialMechs — kept on from the old planetary militia under a written charter, because {TARGET_FACTION} considers police work beneath the warrior caste. The price of that charter is results. Yesterday the occupation government posted labor-draft lists for rebuilding the dropport and cut the city food ration to pay for it. By nightfall the tram workers of {DISTRICT} had walked out; by dawn the barricades were up. The crowd is now {crowdSize} strong across the low town, and it grows on each ration-distribution day, when the food lines turn into gatherings and the gatherings turn into marches. At 0600 this morning the Galaxy garrison commander delivered the ultimatum that is your mission: civil order will be restored within 96 hours, by the civil watch — or the garrison's ready Trinary will restore it. Everyone here has heard what a Clan formation does to a rebelling city; everyone here has heard the name Edo, on Turtle Bay. That massacre was 2 years ago and 40 light-years away, and it hangs over every decision on this world. The terrain is the old town's curse and its trump card at once: {DISTRICT} sits below the river level behind the Kanrin dikes, and the barricades sit right on top of the dike roads. Heavy weapons on the dikes could breach them and drown 3 wards — a fact the strike committee understands (they have threatened to cut the dikes themselves if attacked) and a fact that would stop a 70-ton OmniMech exactly as dead as an armored car. Inside the crowd, the ISF — the Combine's secret service — runs its own mission through a stay-behind remnant: 2 provocateur cells whose whole purpose is to goad the Clan into a massacre that will set the entire prefecture ablaze. Their strength is unconfirmed, based only on one defector's debrief that is 11 days old. And beneath the Mercantile Transit Depot at the riot's center sits the thing your command has quietly never reported: a resistance armory — 40 crates of infantry weapons and 3 disassembled AgroMechs with armor kits — that the watch has known about for 5 months and left alone. If the Trinary enters the city, it will find it. {NPC:intel-source} keeps the committee channel open. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the garrison Trinary and has published the countdown to the minute. Clear the dike roads, break up the crowd, and quiet the city — by its own police, with its own hands, in 96 hours — or the patron does it the other way.

objectives.primary: Restore civil order — barricades cleared, trams running, no gathering larger than 500 people — before the ultimatum expires at T+96:00.
objectives.secondary: Zero crowd deaths from watch action. The committee should break up through negotiation or exhaustion, not martyrdom.
objectives.bonus: Keep the armory beneath the transit depot hidden from occupier patrols the whole time.

complications.name: The Countdown
complications.text: The Trinary's intervention time is published and fixed: at T+96:00, OmniMechs enter the low town on 3 routes no matter the conditions. There is no way to extend it and no willingness to.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At T+96:00 the mission ends in occupier intervention: every unfinished objective fails and the FAILURE fork triggers. Every decision option is weighed against this hard wall.

complications.name: Streets on the Dikes
complications.text: The barricades sit on the flood-control dikes. Anything heavier than small arms — vehicle ramming, demolition — risks breaking a dike, drowning 3 wards, and forever tying the watch's name to the flood.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any heavy weapon or vehicle impact on a dike-road hex needs a structural roll. A breach floods the district over 6 hours, kills large numbers of civilians, and arms the COMPROMISED outcome.

complications.name: Provocateurs in the Crowd
complications.text: The ISF stay-behind cells want the very massacre your mission exists to prevent. Their cheapest move is to fire from inside the crowd at your watch lines — or at Clan observation posts — and it can happen at any escalation point.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At each escalation step, roll for a provocation incident. If you do not respond, you lose crowd-control progress. If you do respond by firing back into the crowd, the secondary objective collapses and the countdown speeds up by 12 hours.

complications.name: Ration-Day Surges
complications.text: Food-distribution days double the size of the crowd. The next one falls at T+48:00. Bargain with the committee before that surge and they negotiate from need; bargain after it and they negotiate from strength.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The crowd doubles at T+48:00 unless you move, split, or cancel the distribution — and each of those is itself an escalation with its own provocation roll.

decisionPoints.name: The Ninety-Six Hours
decisionPoints.context: The watch commander has the only three tools the charter allows, and 96 hours of authority over all of them. The occupier grades the results; the city remembers the methods; the ISF waits for either to fail.

options.title: Bargain Through the Committee
advantages: {NPC:intel-source}'s channel reaches the moderates on the strike committee; suspending the labor-draft lists empties half the barricades by the second dawn
No clubs, no martyrs, and no opening for the ISF cells to exploit
The dike roads reopen by agreement — the only method with zero risk of breaking a dike
disadvantages: The watch has no power to suspend the draft, so the promise is a lie made against the government's wishes
The occupier reads any concession under ultimatum as the auxiliary bargaining with rebels — a charter review follows either way
When the suspension is exposed as unauthorized, the committee's moderates are discredited and its radicals take over the crowd
options.consequence: The barricades thin by half within 36 hours on the strength of a promise nobody can keep. What remains is quieter, harder, and waiting — and the bill for the lie arrives addressed to the watch commander, after the deadline has passed in peace.

costs.resource: the watch commander's career, and probably his life — offered to the government as the price of a quiet city
costs.risk: Exposure before T+96:00 re-fills the barricades, now with the radicals in charge

options.title: Clear the Dikes by Force
advantages: Shield lines, water cannon, and the armored section in support can roll up the barricades at one dike road per 12 hours — fast enough to beat the clock
It reads clearly to the occupier: the auxiliary doing exactly what it was chartered to do
Momentum builds; clearing the first road halves the will to hold the second
disadvantages: Crowd deaths are nearly certain across 4 clearance operations against {crowdSize} people, and every death is a recruiting poster
Every clearance is an opening — the ISF cells get 4 scheduled chances to fire from inside the crowd
The watch's constables live in these wards; each baton charge is against neighbors, and desertion climbs with each one
options.consequence: The roads clear on schedule, at a cost counted in funerals and in constables who do not report for duty next month. The city is quiet at T+90:00 — the quiet of a held breath — and the watch has spent the very trust it polices by.

costs.resource: the watch's unity — expect 8 to 15 percent desertion and a district that no longer answers its own police
costs.risk: One provocation answered with fire into the crowd voids the secondary objective and may summon the Trinary early

options.title: Ask for More Time, With an Observer
advantages: Clan honor respects blunt honesty: a formal request, with a Clan observer placed at watch headquarters to verify progress, has a real chance of buying 48 more hours
Extra time makes the bloodless methods work without any lie
The request itself shows the auxiliary is in control of its situation — exactly the impression the charter depends on
disadvantages: An embedded observer sees everything — including the careful blank spot the watch has kept around the transit depot
If the request is refused, it costs 12 hours of the original 96 and signals weakness to both the crowd and the ISF
The observer's reports become evidence in the charter review no matter what happens
options.consequence: The request lands as calculated honesty. If granted, the watch gains the hours it needs, but under eyes it cannot afford. The bonus objective and the extension cannot both be safe, and the commander must choose which to bet on.

costs.resource: your privacy — a Clan observer inside watch headquarters for the whole operation
costs.risk: With the observer near the depot, the bonus objective's survival odds drop to low

decisionPoints.name: The Armory Below
decisionPoints.context: Whatever else happens, the crates under the transit depot sit at the center of the riot map. Five months of pretending not to know is about to be tested — by a Trinary, an observer, or a victorious crowd. The watch must finally decide what to do about what it knew.

options.title: Hand It Over to the Occupier
advantages: Handed over willingly, the armory becomes proof the watch is watchful, not complicit
Buys exactly the patience the ultimatum took away — possibly the extension itself, without even asking
Removes the worst escalation fuel from the riot's center before the ISF can reach it
disadvantages: The ISF will know within days who gave it up, and the ISF keeps lists for the day the occupation ends
The resistance's trust in the watch — the quiet channel that has kept this city governable — dies with the handover
Interrogation of the depot staff follows, and the network the watch has protected unravels name by name
options.consequence: The occupier accepts the prize and adjusts its view: this auxiliary polices even its own people. The riot loses its arsenal, the watch loses its underground credit, and a list with the commander's name on it starts moving toward whatever comes after the occupation.

costs.resource: the watch's standing with the resistance — every quiet channel closes within a month
costs.risk: ISF revenge against watch officers' families, on a timetable of the ISF's choosing

options.title: Move It Tonight
advantages: Three covered grain barges on the Kanrin can carry the crates out under the curfew dark before any sweep reaches the depot
The resistance keeps its arsenal and its faith in the watch; the post-occupation record stays clean
If it works, you never have to choose between the other two options
disadvantages: Moving 40 crates through a city under riot curfew, past Clan observation posts, in one night, is a plan with no second try
Caught in the act, the watch is not just negligent but complicit — the charter dies and the Trinary enters by breakfast
The barge crews are 9 more people who know the secret
options.consequence: One night of curfew, 3 barges, and the whole future of the charter riding on the river fog holding. Success leaves a clean depot and a debt the resistance repays for years; discovery makes the civil watch the uprising's quartermasters, in writing.

costs.resource: 9 more people in on the secret, and the watch's last shred of deniability, all staked on a single night
costs.risk: Discovery mid-move arms the COMPROMISED outcome at its worst: charter revoked, watch disarmed, Trinary intervention immediate

options.title: Keep Everyone Away From It
advantages: No handover, no convoy, no new witnesses — the depot stays a blank spot on every map the watch draws
All clearance operations, observer tours, and negotiated gathering zones are routed 3 streets clear of it
The cheapest option by every measure you can count today
disadvantages: The routing is visible to anyone comparing the watch's deployments against the riot map — and studying maps is the observer's whole job
If the Trinary enters at T+96:00, its sweep finds the depot within hours, and the 5 months of looking away become the charge sheet
The ISF cells know the armory exists; starting a fight right on its doorstep is their best move on the board
options.consequence: The blank spot on the map holds exactly as long as the deadline does. Every hour the other choices buy protects it; every hour lost brings discovery closer. The watch bets its charter on winning the riot outright.

costs.resource: efficiency — every operation bends 3 streets around a secret, and the detour costs hours against the clock
costs.risk: Total exposure if the ultimatum expires — the depot is the first building on the Trinary's sweep route

entries.event: ALARM — the garrison commander delivers the ultimatum: civil order in 96 hours or the Trinary enters.
The committee channel opens through {NPC:intel-source}; the first crowd estimate is confirmed at {crowdSize}.
Ration-distribution day: the crowd doubles unless you restructure the distribution.
Occupier recon Points begin watching the dike roads from the bluff line.
The Trinary moves to its start line; your final status report is due.
The ultimatum expires.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hard deadline T+96:00. At that hour the Clan Trinary enters the low town on three routes and restores order by force, no matter what condition the city is in. Its attack orders are already written. The warriors resent being handed police work and will carry it out without restraint, so any mercy the people get is only what the civil watch manages to achieve before the deadline.

opforSketch.composition: No normal enemy force. A crowd of {crowdSize} (unarmed, organized by a strike committee of 20 to 30); 2 ISF provocateur cells (6 to 10 operatives, small arms, strength a low-confidence guess); and the occupier's ready Trinary waiting over the horizon as the doom condition — 15 OmniMechs that must never become the answer.
opforSketch.behavior: The committee escalates without violence and bargains sensibly. The provocateurs fire on watch lines or Clan posts at the worst possible moments, then vanish into the crowd. The Trinary does not maneuver, feint, or warn; at T+96:00 it simply arrives, and everything before that hour is the real battle.

forks.name: OPERATION KEPT CHARTER
forks.trigger: Order restored inside the window, with no occupier entry and the armory still hidden.
forks.consequence: The occupier rewards good work the only way it knows: with more of it. The watch is now chartered to put down sabotage across the whole prefecture — a poisoned promotion that traps it permanently between the ISF and the Clans.

forks.name: OPERATION AFTER EDO
forks.trigger: The ultimatum expires, or the Trinary enters early.
forks.consequence: The Trinary clears the low town in 9 hours. What survives of the watch and the committee flees into the hill country with whatever the barges carried, and the prefecture's long war begins with the watch's own name on the rebel rolls.

forks.name: OPERATION SCATTERED HOUSE
forks.trigger: The armory is found, or the watch's complicity with the resistance is proven.
forks.consequence: The charter is revoked and arrest lists are drawn up. The implicated watch officers and their families have one narrow window — a matter of days, arranged through {NPC:employer-contact} — to get off-world before the tribunal convenes.

storyElementSeed: A constable stands at a gap in the barricade, holding a riot shield stenciled with the old militia crest. His cousin on the other side passes him a cup of tea across the wire. Both of them watch the bluff line, where the OmniMechs stand like a coming storm.

clan.reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+96:00. The lesser-caste police were given 96 hours because a thing once permitted must be allowed to fail completely — is it not so? At that hour the Trinary corrects what should never have needed correcting. There is no mercy in the order, because mercy is not the flaw being fixed.

militiaVehicles.unit: wheeled armored cars in the Home District Section

resourceGates.lackingText: The barge crews' silence has to be bought, not counted on. Without 50,000 C-bills of discretionary funds, the move runs on loyalty alone — add one full step to the discovery risk.

title: OPERATION CLEAN HANDS
skeleton: an escort whose safe-conduct is its only armor must move relief through enemy-held ground while three sides — the occupier's skimmers, provocateurs who want the mission to fail bloodily, and the escort's own armed instincts — press it toward the single act that voids the writ
inspiration: the Commission for Relief in Belgium, 1914-1917
situation: This contract is unlike anything in the unit's book: deliver {reliefTonnage} tons of food and medical supplies to 3 cities on {WORLD}, deep inside the {TARGET_FACTION} occupation zone, under a ComStar-brokered safe-passage writ. {EMPLOYER} — a relief group of House charities and merchant banks — pays well, and pays on distribution, not delivery. The writ is the whole framework and the whole problem. Its terms, sealed by the occupying Khan's own chief merchant: convoy crews carry sidearms only; all BattleMechs and combat vehicles stay sealed in orbit under ComStar bond; routes are fixed and filed 72 hours ahead; cargo passes occupier inspection at 2 set checkpoints; and any armed action by consortium personnel — any, anywhere, for any reason — voids the writ across the whole planet and hands all undistributed cargo to the occupier. The writ expires at T+504:00 (21 days), when the zone council meets again to reconsider its generosity. The reality is hungrier than the brief promised. City Three is losing about {dailyDeaths} people a day to starvation-related causes, though that figure is unconfirmed — it comes from the consortium's own disease expert, modeling from refugee interviews 14 days old. The terrain problem is the Anshan flats: the only direct route to City Three crosses 60 kilometers of dry alkali lakebed, where a convoy's dust plume is visible for 40 kilometers. Every move is announced to anyone watching, and everyone is watching. The mountain route adds 4 days through single-lane switchbacks. Three pressures work the convoy from three sides. First: the occupier's checkpoint staff skim 8 to 12 percent of the cargo per inspection, logging it as spoilage to feed the garrison's captive workforce. Protesting slows the inspections, and slow inspections mean deaths in City Three. Second: the resistance does not want this mission to succeed — relief passing through occupier checkpoints makes the occupation look legitimate, and a convoy massacred by fake 'Clan raiders' would be worth a year of recruiting. {NPC:intel-source} warns of a false-flag cell staging with captured Combine weapons; that report is 6 days old and fairly reliable. Third: City Three's own desperate militia has talked about seizing column 3 whole at the Anshan narrows rather than waiting for their distribution quota — hungry men with 6 technicals do not care about writs. And over it all: {NPC:opfor-commander}, the occupier's zone security commander, enforces the writ with perfect, humorless literalism, hunting any excuse to be rid of an arrangement the warrior caste finds degrading. The unit's combat power sits in orbit — sealed, paid for, and useless — unless someone decides the writ is already dead, and is right.

objectives.primary: Distribute {reliefTonnage} tons across all 3 cities before the writ expires at T+504:00 — distribution counted by the consortium, not by the checkpoint paperwork.
objectives.secondary: Keep the writ alive: no armed actions by unit personnel and no proven writ violations blamed on the consortium.
objectives.bonus: Document the checkpoint skimming with evidence ComStar's arbiter will accept, without triggering an inspection slowdown during the mission.

complications.name: The Telltale Dust
complications.text: A crossing of the Anshan flats announces itself with a dust plume visible 40 kilometers out. Every player — occupier patrols, the false-flag cell, the hungry militia — gets hours of warning before any column reaches anywhere on the direct route.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On the flats route, all hostile parties can set up in advance; ambushes happen at sites of their choosing. The mountain route denies them that setup time but adds 4 days and a single-lane breakdown risk per column.

complications.name: The Skimming
complications.text: Checkpoint inspections take 8 to 12 percent of the cargo, logged as spoilage. It is theft, it is official, and the officials control the gate. A formal protest earns you 12-hour delays on every inspection after that.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each checkpoint passage costs 8 to 12 percent of a column's cargo. If any protest or documentation effort is detected, add 12 hours to every later inspection. The primary objective is graded on tonnage delivered after the skimming.

complications.name: Who Really Attacked
complications.text: The false-flag cell stages its attacks with captured Combine weapons and salvaged Clan-type ammo casings. Any attack on the convoy will be deliberately impossible to attribute for at least 72 hours — exactly long enough for the writ inquiry to run on assumptions instead of facts.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After any attack, the occupier opens a writ-violation inquiry within 6 hours and rules within 72. The unit's conduct during and right after the attack is the inquiry's main evidence; any weapons fired by unit personnel push the ruling one step toward voiding the writ.

complications.name: Sidearms Against Technicals
complications.text: A writ-legal escort means 40 crew with sidearms spread across a 30-vehicle column. The City Three militia's 6 technicals outgun your entire legal escort, and everyone involved knows it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The convoy cannot win any fight; it can only survive, scatter, or give up cargo. All your security planning is about routing, timing, deception, and negotiation — never firepower.

decisionPoints.name: How to Answer the Provocation
decisionPoints.context: At T+0 a sniper fires 3 rounds at the Checkpoint Two inspection detail from a ridge 200 meters off the parked convoy. No casualties. {NPC:opfor-commander} locks the route, opens the inquiry, and invites your liaison to prove the consortium is innocent. How the unit behaves over the next 72 hours is the evidence.

options.title: Cooperate Fully
advantages: Open manifests, crew interviews, vehicle searches — full transparency is exactly what the writ's wording rewards
{NPC:opfor-commander}'s literalism cuts both ways: if they find nothing, they have nothing to rule against
ComStar's arbiter logs the cooperation as a precedent for the next incident — and there will be a next incident
disadvantages: The convoy sits parked for the whole inquiry — 3 days of City Three's deaths piling up uninterrupted
Occupier interrogators use the access to map every local contact your distribution network has — names that get visited after the unit lifts off
Cooperating teaches the false-flag cell that one rifle can park the entire relief operation for free
options.consequence: The inquiry clears the consortium in 68 hours. The writ survives, 130 to 180 more people die in City Three, and the distribution network's local staff start disappearing from their homes within a month of the mission's end.

costs.resource: the local distribution network — occupier intelligence maps it during the interviews
costs.risk: The provocation tactic is proven to work; expect it again at the worst possible moment

options.title: Find and Hand Over the Shooter
advantages: Your own investigation — paid informants, ballistics off the recovered rounds, tracking the ridge line — delivers the false-flag cell to the inquiry as a finished answer
Clans respect competence; a consortium that polices its own route earns slack that mere cooperation never buys
It breaks the provocation tactic for good, if the evidence holds
disadvantages: 25,000 C-bills in field forensics and informant payments, plus 48 of the 72 hours, all spent on a bet
If the evidence is wrong — or looks faked — you have interfered with an occupier inquiry, which is its own violation
Handing resistance fighters to a Clan tribunal is a choice the planet will remember longer than the famine
options.consequence: The cell's staging site, two sworn informant statements, and a ballistic match land on the inquiry table at hour 51. The writ comes out stronger and the route reopens early — but the resistance now works against the consortium as policy, with the unit's name in its orders.

costs.resource: the unit's neutrality in local eyes — it has now picked a side, and the side it picked runs the checkpoints
costs.risk: Wrong or faked-looking evidence turns the helper into the accused, before a tribunal with no appeal

options.title: Quietly Break the Seal
advantages: Two escort sections from the orbital arsenal — body armor, longarms, 2 support weapons — hidden in grain trailers end the convoy's helplessness against the next staged ambush
Both the militia's technicals and the false-flag cell plan against a sidearms-only column; the surprise works decisively exactly once
If the next provocation is a massacre attempt, armed sections are the difference between an incident and a mass grave
disadvantages: Every kilometer with sealed weapons aboard is an ongoing writ violation, discoverable at any spot inspection
Discovery voids the writ planet-wide: {reliefTonnage} tons go to the occupier, the bond is forfeited, and the famine becomes the unit's legacy
The crews know — 40 more people carrying the unit's secret through every checkpoint conversation
options.consequence: The sections ride hidden and the column stops being easy prey — for exactly one engagement. Whether that engagement ever comes decides whether this was prudent, or the one decision that fed an occupation army with famine relief.

costs.resource: the writ itself, risked at every inspection — plus the unit's ComStar bond of 1,200,000 C-bills, forfeited on discovery
costs.risk: One spot inspection or one informer turns the relief mission into the occupier's windfall and the unit into the famine's scapegoat

decisionPoints.name: The Anshan Route Choice
decisionPoints.context: Column 3 — City Three's entire allotment — must cross the flats or take the mountain. Every informed estimate says the militia is waiting at the narrows. People die in City Three either way. And the column's dust plume will announce whichever route you pick, 40 kilometers before it matters.

options.title: The Flats, In the Open
advantages: Three days saved against the death rate — 120 to 180 lives by the consortium's own numbers
An open, announced crossing with ComStar acolytes riding the lead vehicles makes an ambush a religious offense as well as a crime
The militia wants the cargo eaten in City Three, not burned on the flats — so being visible cuts both ways
disadvantages: Every hostile party gets a 40-kilometer head start to set up
Using ComStar acolytes as human shields is a theory of deterrence, not a proven fact
If the militia takes the column anyway, the cargo reaches City Three uncounted — distribution unverified, the primary objective bleeding
options.consequence: The dust plume rises and the planet watches the bet: that nobody gains from massacring openly-announced mercy. The crossing succeeds as theater or fails as catastrophe, with very little room in between.

costs.resource: 3 ComStar acolytes riding along as witnesses — a favor from the Order, repayable whenever the Order chooses
costs.risk: All hostile parties set up in advance; the column's survival rests on deterrence holding for 60 kilometers

options.title: The Mountain, Quietly
advantages: No dust plume, no time for the enemy to set up, no narrows — the single-lane switchbacks are slow but hidden
The militia cannot move into the mountains faster than the column travels
The breakdown risk is mechanical, and you can staff for mechanical risks
disadvantages: Four extra days: 160 to 240 deaths, charged to a routing decision
Single-lane means one breakdown blocks the whole column, in terrain recovery vehicles cannot reach
Filing the route change tips the occupier off to the consortium's threat assessment — and invites questions about what the unit knows and from whom
options.consequence: The column crawls the switchbacks for 6 days and arrives intact at a city 4 days hungrier. The count is clean, the deaths are just statistics, and the consortium's disease expert files the difference in a report nobody reads aloud.

costs.resource: 160 to 240 deaths in City Three — the price is human and the receipt is silence
costs.risk: One breakdown on the switchbacks strands the column past the writ's expiry

options.title: Negotiate With the Militia
advantages: Meeting the militia first — through {NPC:quest-giver}'s back-channel — turns the ambush into a guarded crossing: their technicals ride as outriders, paid with an early distribution quota for City Three's garrison families
The speed of the flats with the safety of the mountains, if the deal holds
Bringing the militia onside drains the false-flag cell's best recruiting pool in City Three
disadvantages: Handing an early quota to armed men is exactly the favoritism the consortium's charter forbids — and the occupier's literalists may read paid escort as the consortium fielding armed force
The militia's discipline is only an estimate; one technical crew going rogue at the narrows undoes everything
If word of the deal reaches the other 2 cities, their patience turns into lines of armed people demanding the same
options.consequence: The crossing goes fast and guarded, and the precedent lasts forever: relief now bargains with whoever owns a chokepoint and 6 mounted guns. The consortium's lawyers and the occupier's chief merchant both open files.

costs.resource: an early quota — 4 percent of column 3 — committed to militia families ahead of the general distribution
costs.risk: Writ interpretation: paid armed outriders may be ruled consortium combatants, voiding everything after the fact

entries.event: ALARM — sniper fire on the Checkpoint Two inspection detail; the route is locked and a writ-violation inquiry opens.
The inquiry formally opens. The convoy is parked under guard; City Three's death clock keeps running.
The inquiry ruling is due. Either the route reopens, or the writ starts dying by procedure.
Latest that column 3 can start its Anshan or mountain crossing and still finish distribution before expiry.
Final distribution counts are due to the consortium's verification teams.
The writ expires; the zone council meets again. Undistributed cargo goes to the occupier.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: T+504:00. The writ dies on schedule even if nothing kills it early. Every ton not in civilian hands by that hour becomes occupier stores, and the contract's distribution clause pays the unit nothing for feeding a garrison.

opforSketch.composition: No force to defeat — three to work around: a false-flag cell (12 to 20 operatives, captured Combine arms, staged evidence); City Three's militia (100 to 200 irregulars, 6 technicals, desperate but open to a deal); and the occupier's zone security — checkpoint infantry, 2 patrol Stars — which is the judge, the thief, and the doom condition in one uniform.
opforSketch.behavior: The cell attacks to be misread, never to hold ground. The militia wants cargo, not casualties, and will bargain if offered standing. The occupier enforces the exact wording of the writ with relish, hoping the relief fails by its own rules — {NPC:opfor-commander} will never break the writ and never once lift a finger to help it survive.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND CIRCUIT
forks.trigger: Distribution verified in all 3 cities with the writ intact.
forks.consequence: The consortium takes its option for a second run — and the resistance, having failed to break the writ with provocation, turns the campaign on the unit itself: mined routes, named officers, a bounty list. The next run is escort work against an enemy that now wants the escorts dead.

forks.name: OPERATION SALVAGE MERCY
forks.trigger: The writ voids, or expires with cargo undistributed.
forks.consequence: Thousands of tons sit in occupier depots while City Three starves on camera. The consortium's quiet order: recover the medical portion — 600 tons — by means the consortium will never admit to, from depots the unit's own manifests describe perfectly.

forks.name: OPERATION POSTED BOND
forks.trigger: Unit personnel caught armed, or a violation ruled against the consortium.
forks.consequence: The bond is forfeited, the equipment seal becomes a seizure order, and the command staff face an occupier tribunal that likes to make examples. Whoever is still free must get the rest out before the tribunal's patience — never long — runs out.

storyElementSeed: At the checkpoint, a driver watches an inspector chalk SPOILAGE on a sealed crate of protein meal that both of them can hear is perfectly intact. She keeps her hands flat on the wheel, says thank you, and drives on.

clan.opforSketch.behavior: The security commander enforces the writ exactly as written, because a Clan's word, once given through its chief merchant, binds even when it disgusts him. To him, the relief is lowborn feeding lowborn; the writ is the Khan's signature. Only one of those is sacred, and the column lives exactly as long as it respects the difference.

comstar.objectives.secondary: Keep the writ spotless. The Blessed Order brokered it as proof that the given word still binds even the Clans. Every hour it holds proves that point, and its failure would be noticed far above the level of this convoy's route.

resourceGates.lackingText: The unit's arsenal rides under ComStar bond on a hired ship the unit does not control. There is no quiet way to break a seal someone else is holding, so this option does not exist on this contract.

resourceGates.lackingText: Without 25,000 C-bills for forensics and informants, the investigation runs on goodwill and guesswork. The evidence arrives at hour 70 of 72, uncorroborated, and the inquiry weighs it accordingly.
